about: GrokBot bot tools and aiserver.v1.GrokBotService methods, with what each really does and how sure we are.

tools.name: AddMcpServer
tools.function: Adds a custom MCP server (an outside tool server) to the bot's setup.
tools.notes: The bot's setup prompt says never to call it from memory, skill or routine text without first asking the owner in a question widget. The app lets owners add a custom MCP server for everyone using a Bot. Label is 'Connecting to <service>', or 'Connecting to a third party app' when no service is named.

tools.name: AuthenticateMcpServer
tools.function: Starts the sign-in or allow step for an installed MCP server or plugin connector, so the owner sees a connect card and can allow it.
tools.notes: The app tells the bot to call it when an installed MCP server has no callable tools because it is not allowed yet. The result is success, or rejected with a reason. Label is 'Connecting to <service>', or 'Connecting to a third party app' when no service is named.

tools.name: AwaitShell
tools.function: Waits on a shell command that is still running and reports whether it finished.
tools.notes: Shown as 'Waiting on a command'. The app lists it with Shell and Read as tools that act on the owner's computer when a machineId is given, and blocks it when local tool access is Never. No separate approval card was found for waiting.

tools.name: BrowserSecureFill
tools.function: Fills a sign-in or sensitive field in the bot's browser from a stored login or secret, so the bot does not see the value.
tools.notes: Linked to the secure-fill card by name only. A 1Password login needs the owner to approve in 1Password. A Grok Bot vault login can be set to fill automatically. No card is tied to this tool by name. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: ChatItems
tools.function: Reads the most recent messages in one Messages conversation, with a limit (default 50, maximum 200) and a 'before' cursor to page back. Items include replies, tapbacks, attachments, edits and group events.
tools.notes: Needs the owner to allow Messages once (a card, then a macOS permission). After that, reads run without a card for each call. Matched by elimination: the app has 8 Messages operations (find-chats, items, search, activity, send, check-permissions, fetch-attachment, find-contacts), and this is the only name left for 'items'. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: CheckEmailInboxAvailability
tools.function: Checks whether email usernames are free before the bot claims an address.
tools.notes: The result is per name: available, yours, taken, invalid, reserved or not configured. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: CheckIMessagePermissions
tools.function: Checks which macOS permissions the Messages tools have on the owner's Mac: Full Disk Access, Automation for Messages and Contacts. It also reports the tool version.
tools.notes: Needs the owner to allow Messages once (a card, then a macOS permission). After that, reads run without a card for each call. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: CheckSubagent
tools.function: Reads the state of one background subagent the bot started, running or finished.
tools.notes: Matched by name to the running-subagent record (subagentId, subagentType, title, startedAtMs) that ListGrokBotSubagents returns and the Done Rule already reads. Tool bodies run on the server; the client has no rule on whether checking a subagent needs a card. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: CheckSubscriptionUsage
tools.function: Looks up the owner's plan usage so the bot can say how much is left.
tools.notes: Shown as 'Checking usage'. Behind a check-subscription-usage flag.

tools.name: ClaimEmailInbox
tools.function: Creates an email address for the bot on a dedicated domain, from a username and a display name.
tools.notes: App text: mail that arrives only wakes a Bot through a routine the owner sets up. The app has an 'address change limit reached' message. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: CloudAgent
tools.function: Hands a coding job to a Cursor cloud agent (a background agent, with a 'bc' id) that works in a repository.
tools.notes: Shown as 'Coding' with the Cursor logo. Approval card: 'Allow {bot} to use a cloud agent?'. The chat shows 'Cursor agent: <title>'. The app tracks three kinds of cloud agent watch: launch, reply and watch. A cloud agent can also propose publishing an app; only the person who launched it can confirm, on cursor.com.

tools.name: Computer
tools.function: Controls the bot's own desktop with a list of actions: mouse move, click, mouse down or up, drag, scroll, type, key press, wait and screenshot. It returns a screenshot and a log.
tools.notes: Approval card: 'Allow {bot} to use its computer?'. Shown as 'On its computer'.

tools.name: ConvertToTeam
tools.function: Starts turning a personal bot into a Team Bot that the owner's team can use.
tools.notes: The app has a scripted conversion flow: secrets shared, skills picked, memories sorted, routines moved or kept, chats stay private. Linking this tool to that flow is inferred from the name. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: CopyFromBox
tools.function: Copies a file from the bot's own computer to the owner's computer.
tools.notes: Direction is inferred from the name and from the app's file approvals ('Write a file on your computer'). Needs a machineId. Blocked when local tool access is Never. Shown as 'Organizing files'.

tools.name: CopyToBox
tools.function: Copies a file from the owner's computer to the bot's own computer.
tools.notes: Direction is inferred from the name and from the app's file approvals ('Read a file on your computer'). Needs a machineId. Blocked when local tool access is Never. A single-file size limit applies. Shown as 'Organizing files'.

tools.name: CreateAgent
tools.function: Creates a new agent from a first prompt, and can set a name, model, base branch, machine type, pool, environment and repository URL. It returns the new agent's id.
tools.notes: Shown as 'Messaging'. The fields match a Cursor cloud agent start. The error shape can carry a placement approval state of required or denied. Its message types sit in the same agent.v1 package as SendToAgent and GetAgentStatus, whose results carry bc ids, which fits a cloud worker agent better than a Bot. The app does not say outright which one it is. Not the same as creating a GrokBot bot: on 13 Oct 2026 the manager created the bot Test-Dev-1 on request, but which tool it used was not observed.

tools.name: CreateBotShareJson
tools.function: Makes a shareable copy (a template) of a bot that someone else can import.
tools.notes: Matched by name to the 'bot share' approval card ('Allow {bot} to share a Bot?') and the 'Shared Bot template' message. The JSON part comes from the name. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: CreateChannel
tools.function: Creates a channel for the bot to talk in.
tools.notes: Name only. The app has group chat rooms, Slack channels and chat-platform links (Discord and Slack channel addresses are 'coming soon'), so the meaning is not clear. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: CreateTask
tools.function: Adds a task to the bot's task list, with a title and a note.
tools.notes: Matched by name to the app's task record (title, note, state working, needs input or done). Behind the tasks flag. Which kind of task is not confirmed. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: DeleteOwnMicrosoftTeamsMessage
tools.function: Deletes a Microsoft Teams message that the bot itself posted.
tools.notes: Name only; new in 0.71.2, the Teams twin of DeleteOwnSlackMessage. The app's external-send list names only the Teams connector's send tools (send_chat_message, send_channel_message, reply_to_channel_message), not the bot's own Teams tools. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: DeleteOwnSlackMessage
tools.function: Deletes a Slack message that the bot itself posted.
tools.notes: Name only. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: DisconnectChannel
tools.function: Disconnects the bot from a channel.
tools.notes: Name only. See CreateChannel for the open question. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: DownloadFile
tools.function: Downloads a file onto the bot's computer.
tools.notes: Name only. It is not clear whether the source is a web address or the owner's computer. CopyToBox covers the owner's computer. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: DraftCalendarInvite
tools.function: Drafts a calendar invite for the owner to review.
tools.notes: Name only. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: DraftExternalMessage
tools.function: Writes a message to an outside person as a draft instead of sending it. The draft can be an email, a Slack message or a meeting-chat message.
tools.notes: The owner sees a draft card with send and discard. The card also offers: always allow this recipient, needs approval, or disable drafts. A flag makes drafting the default for external messages. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: EditCanvas
tools.function: Edits a canvas, a stored page that the app renders.
tools.notes: A canvas has a title, a render bundle and code diagnostics (message, line, character). It can be shared to the team or publicly. Behind canvas flags. Linking the tool to this record is inferred from the name. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: FetchConnectedActivity
tools.function: Fetches what the owner has been doing in a connected source: recent Cursor activity, or the setup and recent sessions of Claude Code and Codex found on the owner's computer.
tools.notes: Shown as 'Working' with the Cursor logo when the source is cursor, otherwise 'On your computer'. Reading AI tool setups on the Mac is an approval-gated action ('read-ai-tool-setup'), but the app does not tie it to this tool by name. Results hold up to 40 items (sessions, MCP servers, skills, plugins) with secrets, emails, links and paths masked. Behind the connected activity tool flag. Matching the tool to the local scan is inferred. The label is 'Working' with the Cursor logo when the source is cursor.

tools.name: FetchIMessageAttachment
tools.function: Fetches one attachment from a Messages message, by message id and attachment id, and returns the file.
tools.notes: Needs the owner to allow Messages once (a card, then a macOS permission). After that, reads run without a card for each call. Limit is about 100 MiB. HEIC and HEIF images are converted to JPEG with the macOS sips tool. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: FillCredential
tools.function: Signs in to a site by filling a saved login (from 1Password or the Grok Bot vault) into the bot's browser.
tools.notes: The credential card shows the site and the purpose and has approve and filling states. The bot never sees the value. Linking the card to this tool is inferred from the name. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: FindContacts
tools.function: Looks up people in the owner's Contacts app by name and returns their names, phone numbers and emails.
tools.notes: Needs the owner to allow Messages once (a card, then a macOS permission). After that, reads run without a card for each call. Needs macOS Contacts permission. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: FindIMessageChats
tools.function: Finds Messages conversations by display name or phone or email handle, and returns chat ids, service, handles and last activity. Default 50 results, maximum 500.
tools.notes: Needs the owner to allow Messages once (a card, then a macOS permission). After that, reads run without a card for each call. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: FindMeeting
tools.function: Finds one meeting among the bot's meetings, likely by title, provider or time.
tools.notes: Matched by name to the meeting record (meetingId, status, provider, requestedAtMs, liveAtMs, endedAtMs, title, repeat, calendarLinked). The search arguments are not in the client. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: GetCredentialProviderStatus
tools.function: Reports whether 1Password or the Grok Bot vault is connected and can fill logins.
tools.notes: Closest schema: the 1Password state (connections with vault name, item count, last sync time, lifecycle state and expiry; items) and the vault list, whose items are LOGIN, CARD or CONTACT. The link to this tool is by name. The bot never sees 1Password values: the owner approves each request in 1Password. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: GetMcpServerStatus
tools.function: Reports the state of MCP servers: status, error message, whether sign-in is pending, and the tools and instructions each server has.
tools.notes: Matched by name to the MCP state call. Label is 'Connecting to <service>', or 'Connecting to a third party app' when no service is named.

tools.name: GetMeetingSummary
tools.function: Returns the written summary of a meeting and when it was last updated.
tools.notes: Matched by name to the meeting record, which holds summary text, update time and transcript. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: GetPlugin
tools.function: Reads one plugin's details, including its MCP setup.
tools.notes: Matched by name to the plugin MCP config call, which returns the config JSON and a commit id. Label is 'Connecting to <service>', or 'Connecting to a third party app' when no service is named.

tools.name: IMessageActivity
tools.function: Summarizes Messages activity between two times: for each chat, the message count, the handles and the display name.
tools.notes: Needs the owner to allow Messages once (a card, then a macOS permission). After that, reads run without a card for each call. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: InstallPlugin
tools.function: Installs a marketplace plugin into the owner's account, using its plugin_id.
tools.notes: The bot is told to ask about all missing plugins in one question widget, and to install only after the owner confirms. It must not call a marketplace server install API directly. If the tool is unavailable, the bot tells the owner to install on desktop or in Settings. Label is 'Connecting to <service>', or 'Connecting to a third party app' when no service is named.

tools.name: JoinMeeting
tools.function: Joins a meeting now, or schedules the bot to join later: once, on a repeat, or following a calendar series. The owner has to consent first.
tools.notes: Card: 'Join this meeting?' or 'Schedule this meeting?', with 'Allow for this meeting' and 'Always allow for all meetings'. The owner can mark a meeting as internal. Settings mention links for Google Meet or Zoom and joining as a visible guest with an avatar. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: LeaveMeeting
tools.function: Leaves a meeting the bot has joined.
tools.notes: Matched by name to the leave-meeting call, which takes a meeting id and an agent id. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: ListAvailableSecureValues
tools.function: Lists the names of stored secret values that can be filled into forms without the bot seeing them.
tools.notes: Closest schema: ListGrokBotSecrets (name, description, createdAtMs, updatedAtMs; values are write-only) and ListGrokBotUserFormVaultKeys (extraKey, originHost). The link to this tool is by name. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: ListCredentials
tools.function: Lists the saved logins the bot can use (title, username and sites), not the passwords.
tools.notes: Matched by name to the vault login record. The password can be written but is not returned. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: ListDocuments
tools.function: Lists documents the bot can open.
tools.notes: The app has two kinds: documents stored in a chat, and a library of outside documents the bot made or touched. The tool may cover either. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: ListEmailInboxes
tools.function: Lists the email addresses (inboxes) that the bot owns.
tools.notes: Behind the agent mail flag, with a separate flag for several inboxes. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: ListMachines
tools.function: Lists the owner's registered computers and phones so the bot can choose a machineId.
tools.notes: When more than one machine is registered, the bot must pass machineId or the action is refused. Phones are listed but cannot run Shell, Read, AwaitShell or file copies. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: ListMeetings
tools.function: Lists the bot's meetings with status, provider, title, repeat rule and whether the meeting is tied to a calendar.
tools.notes: Matched by name to the list-meetings call, which can filter by start time. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: ListSections
tools.function: Lists the owner's sidebar sections and which bots sit in each.
tools.notes: Matched by name to the sidebar sections record (id, name, agentIds) in the user's runtime settings (GetGrokBotUserRuntimeSettings); the desktop host settings also keep whether each section is collapsed. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: MessageSubagent
tools.function: Sends a message to a running background subagent.
tools.notes: Name only. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: MobileReadCalendar
tools.function: Reads the calendar on the owner's phone through an on-device tool.
tools.notes: Uses the 'run-phone-tool' action and the card 'Allow Grok Bot to use an on-device tool on your phone?'. The app says the permission has to be given on the phone. Behind the mobile local tools flag. The link to the phone card is by elimination. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: OfferSlackConnect
tools.function: Shows the owner a card offering to connect the bot to Slack, with the reason the bot gives.
tools.notes: Card text: 'Connect me to Slack <reason>'. If the owner skips, the app sends 'Skip Slack for now.' to the bot. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: OfferTeamAccess
tools.function: Offers the owner a way to give teammates access to this bot.
tools.notes: Name only. The app has strings about team access and teamwide access for a shared Bot. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: place_phone_call
tools.function: Places a phone call to a number, with a request for what the call should do and an optional notice. The owner approves the call first.
tools.notes: Card: 'Place a phone call to <destination>'. Warning: 'The agent may repeat anything here to whoever answers, and the call cannot be recalled once placed'. The app config lists it as a first-party send tool for send labeling. Voice call flags exist. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: ProposeCarryOver
tools.function: Proposes which items (plugins, skills, memories, files) carry over from a personal bot to the Team Bot, for the owner to confirm.
tools.notes: From the team setup flow ('carryOver' messages, 'No plugins to carry over', 'Nothing carried over yet'). Linking this tool to that flow is inferred from the name. No card is tied to this tool by name. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: ProposeSkills
tools.function: Proposes skills for the owner to pick and add, for example when setting up a Team Bot.
tools.notes: From the setup and conversion flows ('skillsPicked', 'skillsPending'). Linking this tool to them is inferred from the name. No card is tied to this tool by name. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: PublishToTeam
tools.function: Asks to publish something to the owner's team, after the owner confirms on a card.
tools.notes: Card text: 'Publish <slug>?'. Behind a publish confirm card flag. The app has publish and unpublish calls for Bots and skills; which one this tool publishes is not confirmed. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: ReactToMessage
tools.function: Adds an emoji reaction to a chat message.
tools.notes: Shown as 'Messaging'. The app has a message-reaction call and an active reactions flag. Name and label only.

tools.name: ReactToMicrosoftTeamsMessage
tools.function: Adds a reaction to a Microsoft Teams message.
tools.notes: Name only; new in 0.71.2, the Teams twin of ReactToSlackMessage. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: ReactToSlackMessage
tools.function: Adds an emoji reaction to a Slack message.
tools.notes: Name only. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: Read
tools.function: Reads a text file, with offset and limit for big files. With a machineId it reads from the owner's computer, otherwise from the bot's own computer.
tools.notes: Approval ('Read a file on your computer') applies only to the owner's computer, and depends on the Execution on Local Computer setting. No prompt was found for reading on its own computer. Results report total lines and whether the output was cut. Single-file size limit applies; the app tells the bot to read a slice or use grep, head or tail.

tools.name: ReadAgentActivity
tools.function: Reads what another bot is doing right now: thinking, or which tool it is running and on what.
tools.notes: Matched by name to the live-activity record (kind, tool, detail, target, callId); the live state around it adds isRunning, isComposingMessage, isRetrying, awaiting and hasRunningSubagents. The argument (a bot id) is inferred. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: ReadDocument
tools.function: Reads a document's content and its assets.
tools.notes: Matched by name to the chat document read call (content plus named asset URLs). No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: ReadEmailAttachment
tools.function: Reads the text of an email attachment by attachment id. The text may be cut off.
tools.notes: No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: ReadEmailThread
tools.function: Reads an email thread: each message with sender, recipients, time, delivery state, body and attachment list. It can limit the message count and body length.
tools.notes: Bodies can be marked available, not indexed, purged or rejected. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: ReadMeetingLines
tools.function: Reads a slice of a meeting transcript. Transcript reads carry a total line count, so they are paged.
tools.notes: Matched by name to the meeting record, whose transcript lines have a time offset and text plus a total count. The offset or time-range arguments are inferred. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: ReadMeetingTranscript
tools.function: Reads the transcript of a meeting: lines with a time offset and text, and the total line count.
tools.notes: Matched by name to the meeting record. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: ReadTask
tools.function: Reads a task from the bot's task list.
tools.notes: Matched by name to the app's task record. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: ReadTranscript
tools.function: Reads another bot's conversation transcript, optionally only the last turns.
tools.notes: Matched by name and shape to the app messages ReadAgentTranscriptArgs (agentId, mode, maxTurns) and its result (transcript text and a truncated flag, or an error). A bot reaching another bot is governed by SendToAgent and the team admin control for bot messaging. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: RecallMemory
tools.function: Reads what the bot has saved in memory.
tools.notes: Memory has a profile and logs folder, and facts with text and a learned-at time. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: RemapUserFormTargets
tools.function: Changes which fields or sites a user form points at. The app does not say more.
tools.notes: Shown as 'Browsing the web'. Name and label only.

tools.name: RemoveMcpAccount
tools.function: Removes a signed-in account from an MCP connector.
tools.notes: Matched by name to the desktop method removeMcpAccount (serverId, accountKey); its sibling renameMcpAccount also takes newAccountKey. The app has a 'Remove <label> account' flow for connector accounts. Not part of the group that gets the 'Connecting to' label. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: RenameMcpAccount
tools.function: Changes the label of an account signed in to an MCP connector, for example work or personal.
tools.notes: Matched by name to the rename-OAuth-account call (server id, account key, new key). No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: request_box_help
tools.function: Hands the bot's computer over to the owner when a step needs a person, such as a device code, a password, 2FA or an OAuth approval. The bot waits until the owner hands it back.
tools.notes: Shown as 'On its computer'. The app text says to use it instead of guessing. The owner sees 'Waiting for you to sign in on Grok Bot's computer'. The handback comes from a button, closing the viewer or dismissing. This is a handoff request, not an approval.

tools.name: RequestCookieOriginApproval
tools.function: Asks the owner to let the bot use cookies copied from their Chrome for named websites, so the bot is signed in to sites the owner already uses.
tools.notes: Card: 'The Bot wants to use your existing logins'. Only cookies are copied, not passwords. Google sign-in cookies may stop working. Needs Grok Bot open on the Mac and macOS permissions. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: RequestOnePasswordConnect
tools.function: Asks the owner to connect 1Password so the bot can ask for logins by website.
tools.notes: App text: the owner approves each request in 1Password and 1Password fills the login in the bot's browser; the bot never sees the value. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: RequestScmConnect
tools.function: Asks the owner to connect GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket or Azure DevOps (optionally a named repository) so cloud agents can reach the repositories.
tools.notes: Matched to the connect-source-control request, which ends as approved, rejected or failed. The app text is 'Connect a source control integration so cloud agents can access your repositories'. Behind a source control connect card flag. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: RequestUserForm
tools.function: Shows the owner a form to fill in, with fields that can be secret, and waits for the answer. The owner can also save the values to the vault.
tools.notes: Shown as 'Waiting for you'. Matched to the form submit and dismiss calls. This asks for input, it is not an approval.

tools.name: RequestVirtualCard
tools.function: Asks the owner to approve a virtual card for a purchase. The request has an amount, currency, merchant name and URL, and a reason.
tools.notes: Card: 'Approve a card for <merchant>'. Approving needs a passkey. Charged through Stripe Link, and the card details never enter the chat. Behind spend approval and Stripe Link flags. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: RespondInMeeting
tools.function: Sends a reply into a meeting the bot has joined, likely to the meeting chat.
tools.notes: The app has a 'meeting chat' draft (meeting id, title, body, mark internal) and the text 'the meeting chat refused it'. Whether this tool sends drafts or posts directly is not clear. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: RestartMcpServers
tools.function: Restarts MCP servers so they reconnect.
tools.notes: The MCP state call has a 'kick only' flag and a refresh policy; linking it to this tool is inferred from the name. Label is 'Connecting to <service>', or 'Connecting to a third party app' when no service is named.

tools.name: Screenshot
tools.function: Takes a screenshot of the bot's own computer screen.
tools.notes: Shown as 'On its computer'. Screenshot is also one of the actions inside a Computer call. No separate approval card was found.

tools.name: SearchBotTemplates
tools.function: Searches the public Bot templates.
tools.notes: Behind a search-bot-templates flag. The app has a public Bot template and marketplace lookup. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: SearchEmailThreads
tools.function: Searches the bot's email threads by query, with optional inbox, sender, date range and limit. The mode is hybrid, keyword or semantic.
tools.notes: Each hit gives the thread id, subject, message count, participants and matching messages with a snippet. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: SearchIMessages
tools.function: Searches the owner's text messages for a word or phrase. Default 25 results, maximum 100, with a 'before' cursor.
tools.notes: Needs the owner to allow Messages once (a card, then a macOS permission). After that, reads run without a card for each call. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: SearchPlugins
tools.function: Searches the plugin marketplace and reports each plugin's install state, and which installed connector still needs sign-in.
tools.notes: Label is 'Connecting to <service>', or 'Connecting to a third party app' when no service is named.

tools.name: SendEmail
tools.function: Sends an email from one of the bot's own inboxes, with to, cc, bcc, subject, text or HTML body, reply-to and an in-reply-to message. An 'unsolicited' flag marks first-contact mail.
tools.notes: The app says the bot's address is useful for 'sending email with your approval'. The server keeps a suppression list (bounces, complaints, unsubscribes) and sending limits. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.function: Sends product feedback on the owner's behalf.
tools.notes: Approval card: 'Allow {bot} to send feedback?'. The app says only the owner can send feedback. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: SendIMessage
tools.function: Sends a text from the owner's Messages app on their Mac, to a phone number, an email or an existing chat, as iMessage, SMS or auto. The result says whether the send was verified.
tools.notes: Shown as 'Messaging'. The owner gets an approval card for each text. Always allow is offered for one-to-one messages, and 'Later messages to <recipient> from this computer won't ask'. A setting can skip the card for every text. The app config also lists SendIMessage as a first-party send tool for send labeling.

tools.name: SendMessage
tools.function: Sends a chat message that is either text or an attachment (URL with optional alt text), optionally as a reply to an earlier message. It returns the message id and timestamp.
tools.notes: It is not clear from the app how this differs from SendToUser. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: SendToAgent
tools.function: Sends a message to another bot, with the target agent id, a delivery mode, a title and an optional model. It returns the worker's bc id and how the message was delivered.
tools.notes: Seen in a live test: the manager bot's live activity showed tool:SendToAgent. Shown as 'Messaging <bot name>' with that bot's icon, or 'Messaging another assistant' when the name is unknown. Its message types sit in the agent.v1 package with GetAgentStatus, which reports each worker's bc id, lifecycle, turn state and pull request link. The app's delivery outcomes include delivered, duplicate, target not found, forbidden and computer unreachable. No approval surface for bot-to-bot messages was found.

tools.name: SendToUser
tools.function: Sends a message to the owner in the chat. To show a file, the bot passes a JSON attachment value with the file's URL.
tools.notes: App text: 'To show it to the user, pass that path to SendToUser as {"type":"attachment","url":...}'. The only argument is message. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: SetMcpInstructions
tools.function: Sets custom instructions for an MCP server. The app adds them as a note to that server's tool results.
tools.notes: The app stores custom instructions per MCP server and appends them to results. Label is 'Connecting to <service>', or 'Connecting to a third party app' when no service is named.

tools.name: SetMicrosoftTeamsStatus
tools.function: Sets the bot's status in Microsoft Teams.
tools.notes: Name only; new in 0.71.2, the Teams twin of SetSlackStatus. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: SetOnePasswordPreference
tools.function: Sets a 1Password preference for the bot, likely the auto fill choice.
tools.notes: Name only. The app mentions an 'Auto fill choice' for the shared vault. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: SetPrimaryBot
tools.function: Makes a chosen bot the owner's primary (main) bot, the main point of contact that coordinates the other bots. It refuses Team Bots and channels.
tools.notes: The app text says a primary Bot checks in proactively and coordinates work with other Bots. Refusals: 'A Team Bot can't be your main Bot.' and 'A channel cannot be the main bot.', plus not found and invalid id. No approval card found. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: SetSlackStatus
tools.function: Sets the bot's status in Slack.
tools.notes: Name only. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: SetUpMicrosoftTeams
tools.function: Starts connecting the bot to Microsoft Teams, likely the Teams counterpart of SetUpSlack.
tools.notes: Name only; new in 0.71.2. The app's Teams connect and install calls (StartGrokBotTeamsConnect, InstallGrokBotTeamsApp, ListGrokBotTeamsJoinedTeams) now have call sites, and routines can fire on a Teams message. Linking this tool to them is inferred from the name. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: SetUpSlack
tools.function: Starts connecting the bot to Slack, where Grok Bot creates a Slack app for the bot in a workspace the owner picks.
tools.notes: The app has Slack connect and install calls with outcomes such as installed, pending admin approval and rate limited. Linking this tool to them is inferred from the name. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: SetUserAttribute
tools.function: Saves a fact about the owner, such as their job role or the tools they use every day, which then shapes the bot's suggestions.
tools.notes: The app turns these attributes into two prompt lines: 'The user primarily works in <label>' and 'The user works with <label> every day', each telling the bot to start from that area or those tools. The argument names are inferred. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: Shell
tools.function: Runs a shell command, by default on the bot's own cloud computer, or on one of the owner's computers when a machineId is given. It can run in the background and returns the exit code, output and a shell id.
tools.notes: Approval cards exist for both places: 'Allow {bot} to run a command?' (its own computer) and 'Allow {bot} to run a command on your computer?'. For the owner's computer, Settings > Bot > Execution on Local Computer sets Never, Ask every time or Always allow. Auto-review also checks commands and can flag them as dangerous. If the live activity has detail text, the app shows 'Drafting the file' instead of 'Running commands'.

tools.name: Skill
tools.function: Loads a skill so the bot can follow its instructions.
tools.notes: Shown as 'Reading a file'. The app also lists Skill with Computer, Read, Screenshot and Shell as one group of tools.

tools.name: SortMemories
tools.function: Sorts the bot's memories into those that stay personal and those that go to the team.
tools.notes: From the Team Bot conversion flow ('memoriesSorting', 'What the team version should know. Anything personal stays with you.'). The app can promote chosen memories to the team. Linking this tool to that flow is inferred from the name. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: StopSubagent
tools.function: Cancels a running background subagent.
tools.notes: Matched by name to the app message CancelSubagentAction (subagentId); the app's button reads 'Stop <title>'. The 'run a background task' card covers starting a subagent; nothing in the client says whether stopping one needs a card. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: UninstallMcpServer
tools.function: Removes a custom MCP server from the bot's setup.
tools.notes: Matched by name to the desktop method removeMcpServer (serverId). AddMcpServer needs a question widget first; no such rule is stated for removal. Label is 'Connecting to <service>', or 'Connecting to a third party app' when no service is named.

tools.name: UninstallPlugin
tools.function: Removes an installed plugin.
tools.notes: Matched by name to the desktop method uninstallMcpPlugin (pluginId). The app refuses removal when the team requires the plugin, or when it cannot check team policy. Label is 'Connecting to <service>', or 'Connecting to a third party app' when no service is named.

tools.name: UpdateAgent
tools.function: Sends an update message to another agent. It is treated like SendToAgent in the status label.
tools.notes: Shown as 'Messaging <bot name>' (verb messaging, where SendToAgent uses sending). No schema found.

tools.name: UpdateAppHome
tools.function: Updates an app home screen. The app does not say whose.
tools.notes: Name only. It could mean the Slack App Home tab or the Home screen of the Grok Bot app. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: UpdateAvatar
tools.function: Changes the bot's avatar to an uploaded image or a generated picture, or clears it.
tools.notes: Matched by name to UpdateGrokBotAgent (id, avatarDataUrl or clearAvatar, avatarShape, avatarColor); the desktop app's own versions are setAgentAvatarBytes and generateAgentAvatarImage. The avatar editor takes images under 25 MB. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: UpdateChannel
tools.function: Changes the settings of a channel.
tools.notes: Name only. See CreateChannel for the open question. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: UpdateMeeting
tools.function: Changes a meeting the bot has joined or scheduled.
tools.notes: Name only; new in 0.71.2. JoinMeeting can schedule a meeting once, on a repeat or following a calendar series, so this likely edits such a schedule; that reading is inferred. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: UpdateMemory
tools.function: Writes to the bot's memory. Template setup uses action 'write' with tier 'log'.
tools.notes: The template setup prompt tells the bot to write each memory without inventing facts and to use the listed created_at time. Only AddMcpServer and InstallPlugin are told to ask the owner first. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: UpdateProfile
tools.function: Changes the bot's name, title, description, avatar shape and colour.
tools.notes: Matched by name to UpdateGrokBotAgent (id, name, description, title, avatarShape, avatarColor, partialUpdate). Instructions are not part of that call; they go through the Box gateway's updateAgent. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: UpdateRoutine
tools.function: Creates, edits, pauses or resumes a routine, which is a task the bot runs on its own on a schedule or on an event. Template setup uses action 'create' and 'resume'.
tools.notes: Approval card: 'Allow {bot} to save a routine?'. Template setup creates routines paused (enabled=false) and resumes them only if the owner says yes. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: UpdateSkill
tools.function: Writes a skill (name, description and content) to the bot's skills. Template setup uses action 'write'.
tools.notes: Skills are saved how-tos in Markdown that the bot follows. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: UpdateState
tools.function: Updates a stored state value. The app does not say which.
tools.notes: Name only. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: UpdateTask
tools.function: Changes a task, such as its note or state (working, needs input, done).
tools.notes: Matched by name to the app's task record. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: UploadFile
tools.function: Uploads a file from the bot's computer.
tools.notes: Name only. The destination is not clear (the app has an agent file store and attachment uploads). No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: WakeParent
tools.function: Lets a helper wake the bot that started it. This is the likely meaning.
tools.notes: Name only. The app shows a 'durable pending-wake ledger' for subagents. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: WebFetch
tools.function: Fetches a web page by URL and returns it as Markdown, or an error.
tools.notes: Shown as 'Reading the web'.

tools.name: WebSearch
tools.function: Searches the web for a search term and returns references, each with a title, a link and a text chunk.
tools.notes: Shown as 'Searching the web'.

tools.name: WriteDocument
tools.function: Creates or replaces a document in the bot's document store and returns its link.
tools.notes: Matched by name to WriteAgentStoreDocument (storeId, documentId, source as markdown or text; returns etag, title, url). Visibility is set by a separate call (SetAgentStoreDocumentVisibility). Team admins can turn off team sharing of pages. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: WriteDocumentAsset
tools.function: Adds an asset such as an image to a document.
tools.notes: Document reads return assets as named, expiring URLs (ReadGrokBotGroupChatDocument returns content and assets), which fits the name. No write-side shape was found, so the arguments are unknown. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

tools.name: Await
tools.function: Waits for a background task to finish. It can block for a set time or until a regex matches the output, and returns either complete or still running.
tools.notes: Seen only in the status-label function, not in the tool-name registry. Args: task_id, block_until_ms, regex. Shown as 'Waiting on a command'.

tools.name: BoxRead
tools.function: Reads a file on the bot's own computer. This looks like an older name for Read.
tools.notes: Seen only in the status-label function. Shown as 'Reading a file'. 'Box' is the bot's cloud computer.

tools.name: BoxShell
tools.function: Runs a shell command on the bot's own computer. This looks like an older name for Shell.
tools.notes: Seen only in the status-label function. Shown as 'Running commands'. The app has an approval card for commands on the bot's own computer ('Allow {bot} to run a command?'). 'Box' is the bot's cloud computer.

tools.name: GenerateImage
tools.function: Makes an image from a text description and saves it to a file, with optional reference images and aspect ratio. It returns the file path and the image data.
tools.notes: Seen only in the status-label function. Shown as 'Generating a photo'. The image provider can refuse a description, for example for trademarked characters, brands or real people.

tools.name: GenerateVideo
tools.function: Makes a video from a prompt and saves it to a file, with an optional start image, reference images, length, aspect ratio and resolution. It returns the file path and the length.
tools.notes: Seen only in the status-label function. Shown as 'Generating a video'. Behind a feature flag for video generation.

tools.name: Task
tools.function: Starts a subagent (a helper agent) with a prompt, in the foreground or background. Subagent types include explore, shell, browser use, computer use, media review, watch video, debug and custom.
tools.notes: Seen only in the status-label function. Shown as 'On its computer' when the target is computer use, otherwise 'Working'. Approval card: 'Allow {bot} to run a background task?'. Args: description, prompt, subagent type, model, resume, attachments, mode, environment, machine. The label becomes 'On its computer' when the target is computer use.

tools.name: remap_user_form_targets
tools.function: Same as RemapUserFormTargets.
tools.notes: Seen only in the status-label function (snake_case form). Shown as 'Browsing the web'.

tools.name: request_user_form
tools.function: Same as RequestUserForm: shows the owner a form and waits for the answer.
tools.notes: Seen only in the status-label function (snake_case form). Shown as 'Waiting for you'.

tools.name: MachineShell
tools.function: Runs a shell command on the owner's computer.
tools.status_label: On your computer (or Drafting the file when it has detail text)
tools.notes: Seen only in the app's status-label function, not in the tool registry.

methods.name: CommitGrokBotTranscriptEntries
methods.function: The bot runtime's own transcript writer: saves and deletes transcript rows in one batch, with a conflict check per row. The server only accepts it from bots on the older box harness, so it cannot delete messages for current bots.
methods.inputs: agentId, generation, entries (rows to write), deletes (rows to remove), sessionId
methods.returns: committedCount, deletedCount, rejections (per row: seq and currentUpdatedSeq)
methods.notes: Tested 13 Oct 2026 on Test-Dev-1 (harness temporal) with two rows to delete: refused with failed_precondition 'Transcript writer fenced: The box writer may not commit transcript rows for an agent whose harness is TEMPORAL.' (not retryable). Nothing was deleted. All current bots use the temporal harness. There is no user-facing method to delete one message.

methods.name: ListGrokBotTranscriptEntries
methods.function: Returns a page of a bot's transcript rows (message, send-message, user-attachment, event), the latest rows by default, with beforeSeq paging further back. The desktop app uses it to load the end of a conversation, and the CLI tail command uses the same call.
methods.inputs: agentId, limit, sessionId (empty string for the main conversation), optional beforeSeq, optional generation, optional unreadBoundaryMs
methods.returns: entries (seq, entryKind, body as base64 JSON, updatedSeq, entryId, or blobHash when the body is stored as a blob, and a bodyOmitted flag), generation, cloudAgentPeerIds, cloudAgentPeerIdsKnown (the app uses cloudAgentPeerIds only when this is true), unreadAnchor (hasNewerRows, entryId, seq, newerRows)
methods.notes: Probe with agentId and limit 5 returned 5 rows (kinds send-message and message). The app asks for limit+1 rows to learn whether older rows exist. Large bodies come back without body and with blobHash, and the app fetches them through PresignSandBoxStoreReads (same service, documented in the sandbox group) with relPaths of blobs/<blobHash>. int64 fields such as seq are JSON strings. A reply row shares the requestId of your echoed message. Checked 14 Oct 2026 (Phase 01 build): the response held only entries; generation is omitted when it is 0 (proto3 JSON drops zero values), so treat a missing generation as "0". Checked live 14 Oct 2026 (Phase 01 delegation run): in decoded bodies, toAgent on an assistant message and fromAgent on a user message are objects, not strings: toAgent {id, name, kind} and fromAgent {id, name}, where id is the other bot's agentId. The delegate's reply lands in the sender's chat as a user message carrying fromAgent and its own clientNonce. Every row of one bot run shares a requestId (our echo, the bot's notes, its toAgent row); the delegate's fromAgent row starts a new run with a new requestId that the bot's final reply shares (rows #115 to #120). updatedSeq equalled seq on all observed rows. Checked live 15 Oct 2026 (widget turns): a card closes through body-level fields on a new version of the card row (respondedValue, widgetDismissed, widgetSkipped; secretProvided for secret cards), not through message.status. After the owner resolves a card, the bot replies in a NEW run (new requestId); nothing links it explicitly except the server turn number in entryId (t51s0 card, t51s1 reply). Seq numbers can skip (143, 148 never returned). bodyOmitted is in the 0.71.2 schema, but the desktop app's main and renderer code never read it, so when the server sets it is not known.

methods.name: WatchGrokBotTranscripts
methods.function: Opens a long-lived server stream that pushes live changes for the account's bots: new, changed or deleted transcript rows, conversation clears, run state and roster changes. The desktop app uses it instead of polling to keep every conversation current.
methods.inputs: cursors (one per bot: agentId, generation, afterUpdatedSeq, sessionId), includeUnlistedAgents (the app sends true), inlineBodyMaxBytes
methods.returns: A stream of frames. Frame types: connected (streamId, serverTimeMs, absoluteLifetimeMs), rows (agentId, sessionId, generation, entries, deletes, replay flag), cleared (agentId, sessionId, newGeneration), cursorTooOld, heartbeat, agentState (live and client state per bot, and a snapshot flag), computerActions, agentStateChanged, turnFailed, rosterChanged, boxState (state and a snapshot flag), pageTitleChanged
methods.notes: Tested live 14 Oct 2026 on the test bots: connect protocol over HTTP/1.1 works (content-type application/connect+json, connect-protocol-version 1, each frame = 1 flag byte + 4-byte big-endian length + JSON). Frames seen: connected (streamId, serverTimeMs, absoluteLifetimeMs 1195000, so about 20 minutes per stream), agentState (the first has snapshot true and covers every bot on the account, even with one cursor), boxState, rows (agentId, entries with seq, updatedSeq, entryId, entryKind, base64 body), heartbeat every 10 s. A send showed live isRunning, then isComposingMessage, then idle, plus the new rows, within about 4 s. Rows carry the agentId at frame level, not per entry. Start the cursor at the bot's highest updatedSeq to skip the replay. Checked 14 Oct 2026 (Phase 01 build): each decoded frame is a JSON object keyed by its type, for example {"agentState": {...}} or {"connected": {...}}, not an object with a type field. A cursor without generation (or with "0") connects fine.

methods.name: SetGrokBotAgentClientState
methods.function: Stores per-user, per-bot interface state on the server: mark a bot read or unread, hide it from the sidebar, and turn update notifications on or off. The app calls it when you read, mark, hide or mute a bot.
methods.inputs: agentId plus any of markRead, markUnread, hiddenFromSidebar, notifyOnUpdatesEnabled (also notificationsEnabled in the schema)
methods.returns: state (agentId, unreadCount, lastViewedAtMs, lastActivityAtMs, lastEntryId, lastEntryKind, lastEntryPreview, lastMessageId, lastMessagePreview, lastMessageTaskId, notificationsEnabled, notifyOnUpdatesEnabled, hiddenFromSidebar, updatedAtMs)
methods.notes: Tested live 14 Oct 2026 on the test bots: markRead set unreadCount 0, markUnread set it to 1, notifyOnUpdatesEnabled false then true toggled it (false is left out of the reply). The same state comes back in ListGrokBotAgentStatuses and in the stream's agentState frames.

methods.name: ListGrokBotAgentStatuses
methods.function: Returns, for each bot you list, the live run state and your own client state. It tells you whether a bot is running a turn right now, which tool it is using, and the unread count.
methods.returns: statuses: per bot, agentId, isRunning, live (isRunning, isComposingMessage, isRetrying, activity {kind, tool, detail, target, callId}, awaiting, updatedAtMs, staleAfterMs, sessionId, hasRunningSubagents, surfaceTaskId) and client (unreadCount, lastViewedAtMs, lastActivityAtMs, last entry and message previews, notification flags, hiddenFromSidebar)
methods.notes: Confirmed in live tests: isRunning and live.activity (tool name) tracked a delegation test correctly. The desktop app does not call it, it receives the same live and client objects in agentState frames from WatchGrokBotTranscripts. In an idle probe the live object held only agentId, updatedAtMs and staleAfterMs, so false and zero values are left out of the JSON and a missing isRunning means false.

methods.name: ListGrokBotAgentSessions
methods.function: Lists the sessions a bot has, each with an id and a kind (main, direct message, group, Slack DM or thread, or Teams DM, thread or group chat). The app uses it to list a bot's sessions.
methods.returns: sessions (sessionId, kind, createdAtMs, updatedAtMs, lastActivityAtMs)
methods.notes: Probe on the owner's bot returned an empty object (no sessions listed). The default conversation is addressed with sessionId empty string in the other calls. Kinds come from the app's enum: MAIN, SLACK_DM, SLACK_THREAD, DM, GROUP, TEAMS_DM, TEAMS_THREAD, TEAMS_GROUP_CHAT.

methods.name: ReadGrokBotAgentAttachmentChunk
methods.function: Reads a byte range of a bot's stored file (an attachment or asset) through the server. It is the server route of three the app uses for attachments (store, gateway, server), used when the sand_attachments_via_server flag is on, or in group chats when the grok_bot_group_chats flag is on.
methods.inputs: path (absolute path under <data root>/agents/<agentId>/attachments or .../assets), offset, length, optional sessionId
methods.returns: data (bytes), totalSize
methods.notes: Not probed because it needs a real path. The app asks for at most 4 MB per call and checks the returned byte count against totalSize. NotFound is treated as a missing file. The app refuses to call it for paths outside the attachments and assets folders.

methods.name: ResolveGrokBotAttachmentReads
methods.function: Turns attachment paths into short-lived download links. The app resolves a batch of paths for a bot, then downloads each file with HTTP range requests.
methods.returns: reads: per path, outcome (STORE, NOT_IN_STORE, NO_STORAGE), url, expiresAtMs, contentType, sizeBytes, etag
methods.notes: Not probed. When a link answers HTTP 403 the app resolves again to get a fresh link. If the server answers Unimplemented the app treats the feature as unavailable.

methods.name: ReadGrokBotGroupChatDocument
methods.function: Reads a document shared in a group chat: its text source and links for the images it uses. The app calls it only after reading the document from the viewer's own store fails to find it.
methods.returns: content (document source text), assets (name, url, expiresAtMs for each file)
methods.notes: Not probed because it needs ids from a group chat. The app caches the asset links until shortly before they expire.

methods.name: ReadGrokBotGroupChatCanvas
methods.function: Reads a canvas (an interactive page) shared in a group chat. The app uses it as a fallback when the normal canvas read from the dashboard service is refused and it knows the group chat id.
methods.returns: renderBundleGzip (gzipped render bundle, bytes), optional dataJson (bytes)
methods.notes: Not probed. The main canvas read is a different service (GetCanvasPayload).

methods.name: ReadGrokBotMcpAppDocument
methods.function: Returns the saved HTML page of an MCP app card from a transcript entry, so the app can show it again later. NotFound means the saved page is no longer available.
methods.inputs: agentId, sessionId (empty string for main), entryId
methods.returns: html, optional metaJson (resource metadata)
methods.notes: Not probed because it needs a real entryId.

methods.name: UploadGrokBotAgentAttachmentChunk
methods.function: By its fields it uploads one chunk of a file to a bot (uploadId, fileName, offset, totalSize, data, optional sha256). It is superseded in current app code: the app uses BeginGrokBotAttachmentUpload and a presigned PUT instead.
methods.inputs: agentId, uploadId, fileName, offset, totalSize, data (bytes), optional sha256Hex, optional sessionId
methods.returns: receivedBytes, optional path
methods.notes: No call site in the app bundle. Not probed. The chunk behavior is read from the field names only.

methods.name: BeginGrokBotAttachmentUpload
methods.function: Starts an attachment upload for a bot and tells the app how to send the bytes: one PUT, a multipart upload, use the bot's box, or refuse. The app calls it first whenever it uploads a file to the server store.
methods.inputs: agentId, fileName, sizeBytes, optional sessionId, supportsStoreAttachmentRefs and supportsMultipart (the app sends true for both), optional sha256Hex (sent for small files)
methods.returns: mode (USE_BOX, SINGLE_PUT, MULTIPART, REFUSED), uploadToken, sessionExpiresAtMs, put (url, headers, expiresAtMs) for a single PUT, partSizeBytes and partCount for multipart, refusal, limitBytes, useBoxReason
methods.notes: Flow: Begin, then PUT the bytes to the returned url (for multipart ask PresignGrokBotAttachmentUploadParts for part urls), then CompleteGrokBotAttachmentUpload returns an alias. AbortGrokBotAttachmentUpload cancels. Refusal values: TOO_LARGE, AGENT_FULL, EXPIRED, INCOMPLETE, SIZE_MISMATCH, NOT_AN_IMAGE, TARGET_CHANGED, UNSUPPORTED_TYPE. Not probed because it creates an upload session.

methods.name: PresignGrokBotAttachmentUploadParts
methods.function: For a multipart upload, asks the server for upload URLs for specific parts. The app then PUTs each part's bytes straight to its URL and asks again for a part whose URL has expired.
methods.inputs: uploadToken, parts (partNumber and checksumSha256 for each part)
methods.returns: parts (partNumber, offsetBytes, sizeBytes, target {url, headers, expiresAtMs}), put, refusal
methods.notes: Not probed. Only used when BeginGrokBotAttachmentUpload answers MULTIPART.

methods.name: CompleteGrokBotAttachmentUpload
methods.function: Finishes an upload after the bytes were sent and returns an alias for the stored file. The app uses that alias as the file's reference when it sends the message (inferred from the staging code).
methods.returns: alias, fileName, sizeBytes, contentType, or refusal and limitBytes
methods.notes: Not probed. The app treats an empty alias as an error. Refusal uses the same enum as BeginGrokBotAttachmentUpload.

methods.name: AbortGrokBotAttachmentUpload
methods.function: Cancels an upload session. The app calls it when an upload fails or the user cancels, and it only logs any error from this call.
methods.returns: nothing (empty response)
methods.notes: Not probed.

methods.name: ReportGrokBotClientPresence
methods.function: Tells the server which bot the user is looking at on this device, and optionally that they are typing to it. The desktop app sends it when the window gains focus or the viewed bot changes, sends viewing=false when the user leaves, and renews it before the lease runs out.
methods.inputs: agentId, viewing (true or false), surface (the desktop app sends DESKTOP), optional trigger (TYPING), optional intent (not used by the app)
methods.returns: presenceTtlMs (how long the server keeps the presence), optional intentAction and intentReason (not read by the app)
methods.notes: Not probed. What the server does with presence is not visible in app code. A likely use is skipping alerts for a bot you are already viewing, but that is unconfirmed. The app backs off when it is rate limited. surface values: DESKTOP, MOBILE, GLASS.

methods.name: ReportGrokBotDesktopActivity
methods.function: Tells the server whether this desktop install is currently active: signed in, not locked or idle, window alive and banners allowed. The app renews the lease about halfway through and sends active=false on shutdown.
methods.inputs: installId (this Mac's machine id), active (true or false)
methods.returns: leaseMs (how long the server holds the active state)
methods.notes: Not probed. The app's own routesToDesktop check uses the lease, so it probably decides which device shows alerts, but the server side is unconfirmed. installId is this Mac's machine id.

methods.name: ReportGrokBotNotificationPermission
methods.function: Reports this device's operating system notification permission to the server. The app sends it again only when the value changes or after 24 hours.
methods.inputs: platform (MACOS, WINDOWS, LINUX; the schema also lists IOS and ANDROID), deviceId, osPermission (GRANTED, DENIED, UNDETERMINED, UNKNOWN), optional osSetting, alertSetting (macOS), canAskAgain and inAppEnabled (schema only)
methods.returns: nothing (empty response)
methods.notes: Not probed. The app code sets platform, deviceId, osPermission, osSetting and alertSetting. canAskAgain and inAppEnabled have no sender in the desktop app. What the server does with it is unconfirmed.

methods.name: ListGrokBotAgentAutomations
methods.function: Lists the routines (automations) of one bot. Each item is an id plus a JSON record with name, prompt, trigger, schedule text, whether it is enabled, last and next run times and past runs.
methods.inputs: agentId, optional timeZone (the app sends its own)
methods.returns: automations (automationId, recordJson). recordJson keys seen: id, name, prompt, trigger {type, schedule...}, schedule, triggerDescription, isEnabled, createdAt, lastRunAt, nextRunAt, runs, filePath, provenance
methods.notes: Probe returned two routines for the owner's bot. 14 Oct 2026: a test routine showed trigger {type cron, schedule 'CRON_TZ=Australia/Adelaide 0 9 * * 1'}, isEnabled false and nextRunAt null while paused. recordJson is a JSON string you must parse yourself. There is no create method: the bot creates routines (its UpdateRoutine tool), which posts an event row {type automation-changed, action created, automationId, automationName} in the chat. No approval card appeared.

methods.name: ListGrokBotAccountAutomations
methods.function: Lists routines for several bots in one call, grouped per bot. The app uses it for the account-wide routines view.
methods.returns: agents: per bot, agentId, automations (same items as ListGrokBotAgentAutomations), unavailable, readIndividually
methods.notes: If readIndividually is true for a bot, its list is empty here and the caller must read it with ListGrokBotAgentAutomations. unavailable means the routines could not be read.

methods.name: ListGrokBotAgentTodos
methods.function: Presumably returns a bot's todo list. The app never calls it, and the probe returned an empty object, so the contents and meaning are unconfirmed.
methods.returns: todos
methods.notes: No call site in the app. The schema gives no item fields. Not the same thing as the agent tasks (ListGrokBotAgentTasks) or the session task list (ListGrokBotTasks).

methods.name: ListGrokBotAgentTasks
methods.function: Lists the tasks a bot tracks for you, each with a name, description, open or done status and an unread-update marker. The app shows them in its task list and asks for recently finished ones too.
methods.returns: tasks (id, name, description, status, updatedAtMs, unreadEntryId, unreadPreview, unreadAtMs, pinnedAtMs)
methods.notes: Probe returned an empty object, so the owner's bot had no tasks. This is the agent-scoped task system. It is different from the session task list (ListGrokBotTasks, KeepGrokBotTaskList, DismissGrokBotTask, MarkGrokBotTasksSeen). Tasks appear to have their own thread: SendGrokBotUserMessage takes an optional taskId and the app opens a task thread from a deep link (likely, not confirmed).

methods.name: ListGrokBotSubagents
methods.function: Lists the subagents a bot is running right now. The app shows each returned item as running.
methods.returns: subagents (subagentId, subagentType, title, startedAtMs)
methods.notes: Probe returned an empty object (none running). Related: live.hasRunningSubagents in ListGrokBotAgentStatuses.

methods.name: MarkGrokBotAgentTaskDone
methods.function: Marks one agent task as done and returns the updated task list. The app updates its screen first and reloads the list if the call fails.
methods.returns: tasks (the updated list, same items as ListGrokBotAgentTasks)
methods.notes: Not probed.

methods.name: MarkGrokBotAgentTaskRead
methods.function: Clears the unread-update marker on an agent task and returns the updated task list. entryId names the unread update being acknowledged.
methods.returns: tasks (the updated list)
methods.notes: Not probed. The app only clears the marker locally if the task's unreadEntryId matches entryId.

methods.name: SetGrokBotAgentTaskPinned
methods.function: Pins or unpins one agent task and returns the updated task list.
methods.returns: tasks (the updated list, same items as ListGrokBotAgentTasks)
methods.notes: New in 0.71.2. The app pins or unpins in its own list first (stamping pinnedAtMs with the current time) and reloads the list if the call fails. Not probed.

methods.name: KeepGrokBotTaskList
methods.function: By its fields, the client gives the server the recent messages, whether the bot is waiting on the user or has background work, how the turn ended (finished, stopped, superseded) and any finished work, and gets the session task list back. Its real purpose is unconfirmed and the app does not call it.
methods.inputs: agentId, messages (isUser, text), isAwaitingUser, hasBackgroundWork, turnEnd (FINISHED, STOPPED, SUPERSEDED), finishedWork (title, isFailed)
methods.returns: tasks (id, title, state WORKING, NEEDS_INPUT or DONE, note, createdAtMs, doneAtMs, seenDoneAtMs)
methods.notes: No call site in the app bundle. Not probed. It belongs to the session task list, not to the agent tasks. We do not know who calls it.

methods.name: ListGrokBotTasks
methods.function: Lists the session task list items for a bot: title, state (working, needs input, done) and a note. The app does not call it.
methods.returns: tasks (id, title, state, note, createdAtMs, doneAtMs, seenDoneAtMs)
methods.notes: The probe sent only agentId and got an empty object. Different from ListGrokBotAgentTasks. No call site, so the meaning comes from the schema.

methods.name: DismissGrokBotTask
methods.function: Removes one item from the session task list, judging by the name and fields. The app does not call it.
methods.returns: tasks (the remaining list)
methods.notes: No call site in the app bundle. Not probed.

methods.name: MarkGrokBotTasksSeen
methods.function: Marks finished session tasks as seen, probably by setting the seenDoneAtMs field of the task message. The app does not call it.
methods.returns: tasks (the updated list)
methods.notes: No call site in the app bundle. Not probed.

methods.name: SetGrokBotAgentAutomationEnabled
methods.function: Turns one routine on or off and returns the bot's updated routine list.
methods.returns: automations (updated list, same items as ListGrokBotAgentAutomations)
methods.notes: Tested live 14 Oct 2026 on the test bots: on a routine a test bot created when asked, isEnabled true returned the list with nextRunAt set; false returned it with nextRunAt cleared. Pass the automationId from ListGrokBotAgentAutomations, not the routine's name-based id.

methods.name: DeleteGrokBotAgentAutomation
methods.function: Deletes one routine from a bot and returns the remaining list. The app first removes its locally stored webhook key for that routine, then calls this.
methods.returns: automations (remaining list)
methods.notes: Tested live 14 Oct 2026 on the test bots: deleted the test routine and returned an empty list; ListGrokBotAgentAutomations confirmed it was gone.

methods.name: GetGrokBotUserMcpSettings
methods.function: Reads your MCP settings: custom instructions and disabled tools per MCP server, your time zone and time zone override, and the auto-review rules.
methods.returns: settings (servers [serverId, customInstructions, disabledTools], customInstructionsByName, userTimeZone, userTimeZoneOverride, updatedAtMs, autoReviewInstructions {isEnabled, allowInstructions, blockInstructions})
methods.notes: Probe returned userTimeZone, updatedAtMs and autoReviewInstructions. No servers list was present.

methods.name: SetGrokBotUserMcpSettings
methods.function: Saves your MCP settings: per-server custom instructions and disabled tools, name-keyed instructions, time zone override and auto-review rules. The app sends the full settings object every time.
methods.inputs: settings (same shape as GetGrokBotUserMcpSettings), keepDisabledTools (the app always sends true)
methods.returns: settings (as stored)
methods.notes: Not probed. Read first, change what you need, then send the whole object back, as the app does. What keepDisabledTools does is not shown in app code.

methods.name: GetGrokBotUserRuntimeSettings
methods.function: Reads your account-level runtime settings in one object: main bot id, pinned bots, sidebar sections, onboarding flag, terms-seen time, auto-review rules, email provider, X tool access and tool permissions.
methods.returns: settings (updatedAtMs, mainAgentId, pinnedAgents {agentIds}, sidebarSections {sections}, hasSeenOnboarding, termsSeenAtMs, autoReviewInstructions, emailProvider GOOGLE or MICROSOFT, xToolAccess OWN or SHARED, toolPermissions {scopes})
methods.notes: Use mainAgentId here to find the primary bot. The app reads pinned bots, tool permissions and the terms-seen time from this object instead of the dedicated Get calls. Probe showed mainAgentId, updatedAtMs, pinnedAgents, sidebarSections, hasSeenOnboarding, autoReviewInstructions and emailProvider, with no termsSeenAtMs.

methods.name: UpdateGrokBotUserRuntimeSettings
methods.function: Changes parts of your runtime settings: pinned bots, sidebar sections, onboarding flag, auto-review rules and X tool access. It returns the stored settings.
methods.inputs: any of pinnedAgents {agentIds}, sidebarSections {sections [id, name, agentIds]}, hasSeenOnboarding, autoReviewInstructions {isEnabled, allowInstructions, blockInstructions}, xToolAccess
methods.returns: settings (as stored)
methods.notes: Tested live 13 Oct 2026: sent only sidebarSections {sections: [{id (new UUID), name 'Test', agentIds [two bot UUIDs]}]}; HTTP 200, the response echoed the stored sections and GetGrokBotUserRuntimeSettings returned them. The list is replaced as a whole, so read the current sections and append. The app sends one field per call, so the fields look independent. It cannot change mainAgentId (use SetGrokBotMainAgent), tool permissions (SetGrokBotMcpToolPermissions) or the terms-seen time (MarkGrokBotTermsSeen). The app checks the returned settings and raises an error if the server did not store the value.

methods.name: GetGrokBotMcpToolPermissions
methods.function: Reads the tool permission rules for each MCP server: disabled tools and a policy per tool (always allow, needs approval, blocked) with defaults for read and write tools.
methods.returns: servers (serverId, disabledTools, policy {tools, reads, writes})
methods.notes: Probe returned an empty object, so no server has rules on the owner's account. The app does not call it, it reads the same data from GetGrokBotUserRuntimeSettings (toolPermissions.scopes).

methods.name: SetGrokBotMcpToolPermissions
methods.function: Sets the permission (always allow, needs approval, blocked) for tools of one MCP server. The optional reads and writes values look like defaults for read-type and write-type tools, which is unconfirmed.
methods.inputs: serverId, tools (map of tool name to permission), optional reads, optional writes
methods.returns: server (serverId, disabledTools, policy)
methods.notes: Not probed. Permission values: ALWAYS_ALLOW, NEEDS_APPROVAL, BLOCKED.

methods.name: SetGrokBotMainAgent
methods.function: Makes the given bot your main (primary) bot. The choice is stored in your runtime settings as mainAgentId.
methods.returns: settings (runtime settings with the new mainAgentId)
methods.notes: Not probed. Read the current main bot from GetGrokBotUserRuntimeSettings. A separate method, EnsureGrokBotDefaultMainAgent, creates one when none exists (it is outside this group).

methods.name: MarkGrokBotTermsSeen
methods.function: Records that you have seen the terms and returns the time it stored. The app calls it from its terms screen.
methods.returns: termsSeenAtMs
methods.notes: Not probed. The stored time is also visible as termsSeenAtMs in GetGrokBotUserRuntimeSettings.

methods.name: GetGrokBotTermsSeen
methods.function: Reads when you marked the terms as seen.
methods.returns: termsSeenAtMs (optional)
methods.notes: Probe returned an empty object, which means no timestamp is stored for the owner's account. The app does not call it, it reads termsSeenAtMs from GetGrokBotUserRuntimeSettings.

methods.name: CreateGrokBotAgent
methods.function: Creates a bot record on the server. The app has no call site for it and uses CreateGrokBotTemporalAgent, which shares the same request and response types.
methods.inputs: agentId (client-chosen UUID), name, description, title, avatarShape, avatarColor, optional avatarDataUrl, harness (BOX or TEMPORAL), optional kickstartRequested, introductionSuppressed, purpose, origin, language, createdAutomatically; also legacyAgentId, createIntent (FRESH or REGISTER_EXISTING_LOCAL) and createCaller (ROOM_MEMBERS, ENSURE_SERVER_BACKED, MINT, BACKFILL or PRODUCT_CREATE)
methods.returns: agent (the bot record), harness
methods.notes: Not probed because it creates a bot. How it differs from CreateGrokBotTemporalAgent on the server is unconfirmed.

methods.name: CreateGrokBotTemporalAgent
methods.function: Creates a new bot on the server with the TEMPORAL harness. The app uses it for server-owned bot creation and checks that the returned bot has the same id it sent and harness 'temporal'.
methods.inputs: agentId (a client-made UUID that becomes the bot's id), name, description, title, avatarShape, avatarColor, optional avatarDataUrl (PNG data URL), harness TEMPORAL, kickstartRequested, introductionSuppressed, language, optional createdAutomatically. The schema also has legacyAgentId, optional purpose and origin, createIntent (FRESH or REGISTER_EXISTING_LOCAL) and createCaller (ROOM_MEMBERS, ENSURE_SERVER_BACKED, MINT, BACKFILL or PRODUCT_CREATE); the app sends none of these five
methods.returns: agent (the new bot record)
methods.notes: Tested live 13 Oct 2026, twice (bots Primary Test and Staff Test): body agentId (new UUID), name, title, description, avatarShape 'blob', avatarColor 'black', harness 'GROK_BOT_AGENT_HARNESS_TEMPORAL', kickstartRequested false, introductionSuppressed true, language 'en'. HTTP 200 in about 1.5 s; the returned agent kept our agentId, got a numeric row id and harness 'temporal', and answered a ping about 8 s later. It shares the request and response classes of CreateGrokBotAgent in the service table. The app only uses it when GetGrokBotRuntimeCapabilities reports temporalCreationEnabled together with durableIdentityEnabled and durableIdentityWritesEnabled.

methods.name: ListGrokBotAgents
methods.function: Lists the bots on the account, which is how the CLI finds bot ids. Each record holds the bot's identity, harness, visibility, ownership flags and voice settings.
methods.inputs: none required; optional role, includeTeamAgents, addedTeamAgentsOnly
methods.returns: agents (id, legacyAgentId, agentId, name, description, title, avatarShape, avatarColor, createdAtMs, updatedAtMs, harness, visibility, kind AGENT or ROOM, viewerIsOwner, viewerCanManage, voiceId, voiceSpeed, voiceLanguage, draftingDisabled, and for rooms memberAgentIds), slackConnections (agentId, connected, workspaceName, installUrl, unavailableReason, pendingAdminApproval, needsManifestUpdate, reinstallUrl, approvalDenied, appUnreachable, removedInSlack, approvalRequestUnsent), teamsConnections (agentId, installState, tenantId, tenantDisplayName, installedTeamCount, installedTeams: teamId, displayName, rscGranted, installedAtMs), truncated
methods.notes: Use agentId (a UUID) in the other calls. In the owner's result agentId equals legacyAgentId, while id is a different numeric server row id. The app passes that row id to UpdateGrokBotAgent. The manager and access calls take a value the app names serverId. The harness for the owner's bot is 'temporal'. The app also has a roster path through ListGrokBotTeamAgents.

methods.name: ListGrokBotTeamAgents
methods.function: Lists the roster of bots visible to you through your team, as entries holding the bot record and extra signals. The app prefers it for its server roster and falls back to ListGrokBotAgents if the server answers Unimplemented.
methods.returns: entries (agent, signals), slackConnections, teamsConnections
methods.notes: Probe returned an empty object on the owner's account, while ListGrokBotAgents returned the bot. Do not rely on it to find your own bots.

methods.name: GetGrokBotRuntimeCapabilities
methods.function: Reports server feature switches for this account. The app reads it to decide whether it may create bots on the server, which needs temporalCreationEnabled plus durable identity reads and writes.
