methods.returns: capabilities (durableIdentityEnabled, durableIdentityWritesEnabled, temporalCreationEnabled, agentMessagingEnabled, serverRoomsEnabled)
methods.notes: All five flags were true in the probe. If the server answers Unimplemented the app ignores capabilities and uses its own feature gates. agentMessagingEnabled and serverRoomsEnabled have no reader in this app version.

methods.name: ListDeletedGrokBotAgentIds
methods.function: Takes bot ids and presumably returns the ones the server knows as deleted. The app never calls it.
methods.returns: agentIds (the subset reported as deleted)
methods.notes: Returns only those of the given ids that are deleted. Confirmed 13 and 14 Oct 2026 with Test-Dev-1, a throwaway bot and a test room. The app never calls it.

methods.name: SetGrokBotAgentVisibility
methods.function: Sets whether a bot is private to its owner or shared with the team. The app calls it from its sharing controls.
methods.inputs: agentId, visibility (OWNER or TEAM), personalSecretNames (the app sends an empty list unless given)
methods.returns: agent (updated record), outcome (UPDATED, UNSUPPORTED_HARNESS, NO_TEAM, BUSY)
methods.notes: Not probed. Needs a team (NO_TEAM otherwise) and a supported harness. What personalSecretNames does is not visible in app code, it is probably secrets kept personal when sharing, which is unconfirmed.

methods.name: CloneGrokBotAgentToTeam
methods.function: Clones a bot into a team-owned copy. The outcome says whether it was cloned, unsupported, or there is no team.
methods.inputs: agentId, offerEntryId (probably a transcript entry id, its role is not shown in app code), personalSecretNames, inPlace (the app does not send it)
methods.returns: outcome (CLONED, UNSUPPORTED, NO_TEAM), agent (the clone)
methods.notes: Not probed. The meaning of inPlace and personalSecretNames is unconfirmed.

methods.name: PublishGrokBotAgent
methods.function: Marks a team-shared bot as published, and only works for bots shared with the team. What publishing changes for teammates is not shown in app code.
methods.returns: agent, outcome (PUBLISHED, ALREADY_PUBLISHED, NOT_SHARED, UNSUPPORTED_HARNESS)
methods.notes: Not probed. The app shows a published flag only for bots whose visibility is TEAM.

methods.name: UnpublishGrokBotAgent
methods.function: Removes the published mark from a team-shared bot.
methods.returns: agent, outcome (UNPUBLISHED, NOT_PUBLISHED, NOT_SHARED, UNSUPPORTED_HARNESS)
methods.notes: Not probed.

methods.name: AddGrokBotAgentManager
methods.function: Makes a teammate (by numeric user id) a manager of a bot.
methods.inputs: agentId (the app fills it with a value its wrapper calls serverId), userId (integer)
methods.returns: nothing (empty response)
methods.notes: Not probed. Used in the app's team bot management screens. The desktop wrapper names this argument serverId, the numeric row id kept on the bot record next to the agentId UUID. It was not traced to the exact screen, so which of the two ids the server requires is unconfirmed.

methods.name: RemoveGrokBotAgentManager
methods.function: Removes a teammate (by numeric user id) as a manager of a bot.
methods.inputs: agentId (the app fills it with a value its wrapper calls serverId), userId (integer)
methods.returns: nothing (empty response)
methods.notes: Not probed. Same id note as AddGrokBotAgentManager: the wrapper calls the value serverId, and the exact id the server requires is unconfirmed.

methods.name: ListGrokBotAgentManagers
methods.function: Lists the user ids that manage a bot.
methods.inputs: agentId (the app fills it with a value its wrapper calls serverId)
methods.returns: managerUserIds (integers)
methods.notes: Probe with the UUID returned an empty object, meaning no managers for the owner's bot. The desktop wrapper names this argument serverId, the numeric row id kept on the bot record next to the agentId UUID. It was not traced to the exact screen, so which of the two ids the server requires is unconfirmed.

methods.name: AddGrokBotAgentAccessPrincipal
methods.function: Adds one access principal (a type and an id) to a bot. It is superseded in current app code, which edits access with GetGrokBotAgentAccess and UpdateGrokBotAgentAccess instead.
methods.returns: nothing (empty response)
methods.notes: No call site in the app bundle. Not probed. Purpose beyond the field names is unconfirmed.

methods.name: RemoveGrokBotAgentAccessPrincipal
methods.function: Removes one access principal from a bot. It is superseded in current app code, which uses UpdateGrokBotAgentAccess.
methods.returns: nothing (empty response)
methods.notes: No call site in the app bundle. Not probed.

methods.name: ListGrokBotAgentAccessPrincipals
methods.function: Lists the access principals of a bot, with the creator's user id and whether the whole-team row is on. It is superseded in current app code by GetGrokBotAgentAccess.
methods.returns: principals, creatorUserId, teamRowOn
methods.notes: Probe on the owner's bot failed with failed_precondition (custom error). The message is cut off in our probe record at 'Not av'. This is likely a team-only feature, but that is unconfirmed. No call site in the app.

methods.name: GetGrokBotAgentAccess
methods.function: Reads who can use a team-shared bot: a list of entries (the whole team, a user id or a group id, each with role USER or MANAGER) plus which roles can be assigned, whether groups are on, whether the team row may be turned off, and a state token.
methods.inputs: agentId (the app fills it with a value its wrapper calls serverId), listsCrossTierPrincipals (true or false; the app does not send it)
methods.returns: state (principals [team, userId or groupId, role], teamRowOn, availableRoles, groupsEnabled, teamRowOffAllowed, expectedStateToken, crossTeamSharingEnabled, callerMayEditCrossTeamRows), creatorUserId, deletedGroupIds
methods.notes: Probe on the owner's bot failed with failed_precondition. The message is cut off in our probe record at 'Not av'. It is likely a team-only feature, but that is unconfirmed. The function itself comes from the app code, which calls it in its sharing screen. The wrapper calls the id argument serverId (see AddGrokBotAgentManager).

methods.name: UpdateGrokBotAgentAccess
methods.function: Replaces the access list of a team-shared bot with the entries you send, carrying the expectedStateToken from GetGrokBotAgentAccess. If the state changed meanwhile, the server answers Aborted with a retryable flag and the app reloads.
methods.inputs: agentId (the app fills it with a value its wrapper calls serverId), update {principals [team, userId or groupId, role USER or MANAGER], expectedStateToken}
methods.returns: state (same as GetGrokBotAgentAccess), creatorUserId, deletedGroupIds
methods.notes: Not probed. Send the full list: the app builds it from the current entries, and it refuses to edit when it cannot read an entry because an update would drop it. The wrapper calls the id argument serverId (see AddGrokBotAgentManager).

methods.name: GetGrokBotAgentLinkAccess
methods.function: Checks whether you may open a bot someone linked you to. The app calls it for a deep link to a bot that is not in your roster, to choose the message to show.
methods.returns: access (ALLOWED, NO_ACCESS or NOT_FOUND)
methods.notes: Probe on the owner's own bot returned GROK_BOT_AGENT_LINK_ACCESS_ALLOWED.

methods.name: UpdateGrokBotAgent
methods.function: Edits a bot's name, description, title and avatar. In this app version it is used for teammates' bots (viewerIsOwner false), always with partialUpdate true so only the fields sent change.
methods.inputs: id (the bot's server row id, called serverId, not the UUID), optional name, description, title, avatarShape, avatarColor, either clearAvatar or avatarDataUrl (PNG data URL), partialUpdate
methods.returns: agent (updated record)
methods.notes: Not probed. The id here is GrokBotAgent.id (a numeric row id), unlike SetGrokBotAgentVoice and DeleteGrokBotAgent, which receive the agentId UUID. How the app edits its own bots' identity is not through this call in the code we traced.

methods.name: SetGrokBotAgentVoice
methods.function: Sets a bot's voice: voice id, speed and language. The same values appear on the bot record in ListGrokBotAgents.
methods.inputs: id (the bot's agentId UUID), optional voiceId (empty clears it), voiceSpeed, voiceLanguage
methods.returns: agent (updated record)
methods.notes: Not probed.

methods.name: DeleteGrokBotAgent
methods.function: Deletes a bot. The app calls it with the bot's agentId UUID in the id field.
methods.returns: nothing (empty response)
methods.notes: Tested live 14 Oct 2026 on the test bots: deleted a throwaway bot and a test room with {id: <agentId UUID>}; HTTP 200 with an empty body. Both vanished from ListGrokBotAgents, ListDeletedGrokBotAgentIds returned them, and a later send to the deleted bot gave 404 'Grok Bot agent not found.'

methods.name: SendGrokBotUserMessage
methods.function: Sends a user message to a bot. The server accepts and dispatches it, the app counts ACCEPTED_BOX, ACCEPTED_TEMPORAL and DUPLICATE as accepted, and the reply arrives later as transcript rows.
methods.inputs: agentId, messageId (client UUID, echoed back as clientNonce), text, sentAtMs, sessionId (empty string for main); optional richText, replyToId, isFork, attachmentPaths and attachmentNames, taskId, source, sendSource, initiator, enterEpochMs, composedAtMs, traceparent, machineId, mcpConfigJson, onePasswordAppInstalled
methods.returns: dispatched, mode, workflowId, delivery (ACCEPTED_BOX, ACCEPTED_TEMPORAL, DUPLICATE, REFUSED), refusal (failureCode, message)
methods.notes: Confirmed in live tests: it dispatches the message and the bot replies via transcript rows. source is the client surface (DESKTOP, MOBILE, GLASS), not a content source. sendSource is CHAT, PUSH, APP_INTENT or ACTION_BUTTON_DICTATION. initiator is USER, TEMPLATE_IMPORT, TEMPLATE_SHARE, CARD_ACTION, PLUGIN_SETUP or TEACH_RECORDING. The app also counts DUPLICATE as accepted, which suggests the server de-duplicates on messageId (unconfirmed). If the call fails with Unavailable and no retry-after, the app checks GetGrokBotSendStatus and re-sends only if the result is NOT_FOUND. int64 fields are JSON strings.

methods.name: GetGrokBotSendStatus
methods.function: Looks up whether the server received a specific message, by messageId. The app uses it after a send fails with an unclear network error, to decide whether it is safe to send again.
methods.inputs: agentId, messageId (the id used in SendGrokBotUserMessage), sessionId
methods.returns: status (NOT_FOUND, ACCEPTED, REJECTED, PENDING, UNKNOWN_DURABILITY), echoEntryId, rejectionCode, acceptedAtMs
methods.notes: Confirmed in live tests: the status stays ACCEPTED even after the reply, so it reports acceptance only. 14 Oct 2026: an unknown messageId returns status GROK_BOT_SEND_STATUS_NOT_FOUND. Use the transcript or ListGrokBotAgentStatuses to see completion.

methods.name: InterruptGrokBotAgentRun
methods.function: Stops the bot's current run if there is one. The app calls it when the user interrupts a run.
methods.inputs: agentId, reason (the app sends user_interrupt), optional sessionId
methods.returns: hadActiveRun (true if a run was active)
methods.notes: Tested live 14 Oct 2026 on the test bots: during a long counting turn it returned hadActiveRun true; the bot was idle within 5 s and posted nothing more. The CLI interrupt command uses this call.

methods.name: StartFreshGrokBotConversation
methods.function: Starts a new conversation with the bot in place of the current one. The app offers it as a 'Start fresh' action on error cards, for example when the conversation is too large to continue or its saved history is out of sync.
methods.returns: nothing (empty response)
methods.notes: Tested live 14 Oct 2026 on the test bots: on a healthy chat it was refused with failed_precondition 'This action is no longer available. Reset is not available for this conversation.' Nothing changed. It only applies when the app offers 'Start fresh' on an error card.

methods.name: RollBackGrokBotConversation
methods.function: Rolls the conversation back past the failed or blocked turn so the user can edit and resend it. The app calls it from an 'Edit' action on an error card and then puts the blocked message text back into the composer.
methods.returns: nothing (empty response)
methods.notes: Tested live 14 Oct 2026 on the test bots: on a healthy chat it was refused with failed_precondition 'This action is no longer available. Removing blocked messages is not available for this conversation.' Nothing changed. It only applies to a failed or blocked turn, as the app's error card suggests.

methods.name: ListGrokBotAgentMeetings
methods.function: Lists the meetings of one team bot that the caller is allowed to see, plus the bot's current visibility setting. The team bot meetings panel loads it on open and asks again after a change.
methods.inputs: agentId (the bot), fresh (the app sends false on first load and true after a change).
methods.returns: visible (whether the caller may see the list), meetings (meetingId, agentId, status, provider, requestedAtMs, liveAtMs, endedAtMs, title, repeat, calendarLinked), visibility (managers or everyone), ownMeetingIds (meetings the caller owns).
methods.notes: Probe without an agentId returned 404 not_found, which means a required id was missing, not that the feature is off. Statuses seen in the app: SCHEDULED, JOINING, LIVE, ENDED, FAILED, CANCELLED. Providers: GOOGLE_MEET, ZOOM, MICROSOFT_TEAMS. The panel only shows a Cancel or Leave button for meetings listed in ownMeetingIds. Time fields are int64, so they arrive as JSON strings. The setter SetGrokBotAgentMeetingsVisibility is gone in 0.71.2, but the response still carries visibility and team admins have a meetings control; where the per-bot setting moved is not visible in the client.

methods.name: SetGrokBotAgentDraftingDisabled
methods.function: Turns drafting off or on for one bot. The app offers it as the 'disable-drafts' choice on the draft approval card, next to 'always-allow' and 'needs-approval', and the setting is stored on the bot as draftingDisabled.
methods.inputs: id (the bot's agentId; the field is named id, not agentId), disabled (true or false).
methods.returns: Nothing (empty response).
methods.notes: Confidence is medium because the app code shows the switch but not what the bot does differently while drafting is off. The card option is only shown for a single bot that the viewer owns, not for group chats. Not called in the probe run.

methods.name: StartGrokBotImagePrecaption
methods.function: Asks the server to caption an image you attached while you are still typing, so the caption can be ready by the time you send. The composer calls it a short delay after an image is staged.
methods.inputs: image (the image bytes), mimeType, draftText (what you typed so far), priorUserMessages (earlier user messages), agentId.
methods.returns: outcome (CAPTIONED, ALREADY_CAPTIONED, NOT_NEEDED, SKIPPED, FAILED or SKIPPED_FOR_AGENT), contentSha256 (hash of the image).
methods.notes: The app debounces the call, only sends supported image types under a size cap, and cancels it if you send before it fires. After a SKIPPED outcome the app waits a while before trying again. It uploads the image content to the server, so treat it as a write with a privacy cost. Not called in the probe run.

methods.name: GetGrokBotCloudAgentWatchers
methods.function: Lists which bots are registered to watch one cloud agent, identified by its bcId. Each watcher has a kind (LAUNCH, REPLY or WATCH), a durable flag, a registration time and a wake count.
methods.returns: watchers (agentId, kind, durable, registeredAtMs, wakes).
methods.notes: The plain call returned 400 invalid_argument, so it needs a real bcId. The desktop app does not call it. The app does not explain what a wake counts, so that part of the meaning is a guess from the field name.

methods.name: RespondGrokBotWidget
methods.function: Sends your answer to a widget the bot showed in the chat, for example a question with options. The answer goes in as one string.
methods.inputs: agentId, entryId (the widget message), value (your answer as text), sessionId (in the schema, but the app does not send it).
methods.returns: accepted (true or false), refusal (failureCode and message) when the server refuses.
methods.notes: Tested live 14 Oct 2026 on the test bots: value 'Blue' on an open widget card returned accepted true; the card gained respondedValue 'Blue' and the bot replied 'Got it, Blue.' in a new run within about 8 s. Widget body: message.widget {prompt, options [{label}]}. The bot shows one when asked to use its question widget.

methods.name: ResolveGrokBotCredentialRequest
methods.function: Tells the server whether you approved or denied a bot's request to use a saved credential, such as a login held in a connected password manager.
methods.inputs: agentId, entryId (the request card), resolution (APPROVED or DENIED), sessionId (optional).
methods.returns: accepted (true or false), refusal (failureCode and message) when refused.
methods.notes: The desktop app has separate local calls (approveCredentialRequest and denyCredentialRequest, with credentialId, connectionId and targetSite) that handle the credential itself, so this RPC appears to report only the decision. Related UI text says a filled value is never shown to the bot and is entered directly on the site. Not called in the probe run.

methods.name: DismissGrokBotWidget
methods.function: Closes a widget without answering it, so it no longer waits for a reply.
methods.inputs: agentId, entryId (the widget message), sessionId (in the schema, but the app does not send it).
methods.returns: accepted (true or false), refusal (failureCode and message) when refused.
methods.notes: Tested live 14 Oct 2026 on the test bots: returned accepted true; the card gained widgetDismissed true (older cards use widgetSkipped). The bot did not post a reply.

methods.name: SendGrokBotDraft
methods.function: Approves a draft the bot wrote and sends it. The draft can be an email, a Slack message or a meeting chat message, and the request carries the final text, so edits made before sending go with it.
methods.inputs: agentId, entryId (the draft message), exactly one of email (from, to, cc, subject, body), slack (workspace, target, thread, body) or meetingChat (meetingId, meetingTitle, body, markInternal), shownSignatureHtml (optional), sessionId (optional).
methods.returns: accepted (true or false), refusal (failureCode and message) when refused.
methods.notes: This sends a real message to outside people and cannot be recalled. From its name, shownSignatureHtml is the signature HTML that was shown in the preview. Not called. 14 Oct 2026: no draft could be made on the test bots because no Gmail or Outlook connector is set up.

methods.name: DiscardGrokBotDraft
methods.function: Throws away a draft the bot wrote, without sending it.
methods.returns: accepted (true or false), refusal (failureCode and message) when refused.
methods.notes: Tested live 14 Oct 2026 on the test bots: returned HTTP 200 with an empty body both for a made-up entryId and for a normal text row, and changed nothing, so it does not report a wrong id. A real draft could not be made: the test bot said DraftExternalMessage needs a Gmail or Outlook connector.

methods.name: ReactToGrokBotMessage
methods.function: Adds an emoji reaction from you to a message in a chat with a bot.
methods.returns: refusal (failureCode and message) only when the server refuses. A success has no fields.
methods.notes: This is the user side. A bot reacting to a message uses its own ReactToMessage tool, which is a different path. Not called in the probe run.

methods.name: VoteGrokBotFeedback
methods.function: Records an up or down vote on a bot message. After a down vote the app opens a follow-up dialog, and SUBMIT sends the categories you ticked and your comment. REVERT undoes the vote.
methods.inputs: agentId, entryId (the message), action (UP, DOWN, SUBMIT or REVERT), categories (list of strings), comment (optional), sessionId (optional).
methods.returns: refusal (failureCode and message) only when the server refuses. A success has no fields.
methods.notes: The category names are not visible in the app code (they come from translated UI text). Not called in the probe run.

methods.name: SendGrokBotAgentMessage
methods.function: Sends a text message from one bot to another bot. The reply says how it was delivered (through the server-run Temporal harness or the target's box) or why it was refused.
methods.inputs: fromAgentId, toAgentId, messageId (a client-made id; the DUPLICATE result suggests it guards against repeats), text, sentAtMs (int64, so a JSON string), replyToId (optional).
methods.returns: delivery (DELIVERED_TEMPORAL, DELIVERED_BOX, DUPLICATE, TARGET_NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN, BOX_UNREACHABLE, TEMPORAL_UNAVAILABLE or INVALID_TARGET), targetAgentId, targetName, workflowId (optional).
methods.notes: Tested live 14 Oct 2026 on the test bots: fromAgentId Primary Test, toAgentId Staff Test: delivery DELIVERED_TEMPORAL with targetAgentId (numeric row id) and targetName. Re-sending the same messageId gave DUPLICATE, so it de-duplicates. The target saw a user message with fromAgent {id, name} and answered with an assistant row carrying toAgent; that reply landed in the sender's chat as a user message with fromAgent and did not start a turn there. So the CLI can message one bot as another bot.

methods.name: ResolveGrokBotAutoReviewApproval
methods.function: Answers an Auto-review approval card. The app shows one when a bot action was flagged as risky: a shell command (on the host computer or in the bot's box), an MCP tool call, a phone call, a meeting join, or another sensitive action. You approve, deny, or always allow.
methods.inputs: agentId, requestId (message.approval.requestId; no entryId), resolution (GROK_BOT_AUTO_REVIEW_APPROVAL_RESOLUTION_APPROVED, _DENIED or _ALWAYS), approvalPlatform ('desktop'), approvedCommand (optional), sessionId (optional).
methods.returns: dispatched (whether the answer was handed on), workflowId (optional).
methods.notes: Tested live 14 Oct 2026 on Staff Test with the account's allow rule removed for the test (restored after). The card is a send-message row with message.type auto-review-approval and message.approval {requestId, status pending, surface (box_shell), summary, summaryCopy, reason, command, proposedRule}; while it waits, ListGrokBotAgentStatuses shows live.awaiting {tabId 'auto-review', reason}. Body: agentId, requestId (from approval.requestId, no entryId), resolution GROK_BOT_AUTO_REVIEW_APPROVAL_RESOLUTION_DENIED / _APPROVED / _ALWAYS, approvalPlatform 'desktop'. Each returned dispatched true with a workflowId. DENIED: card status denied, the command did not run, the bot reported it. APPROVED: card status approved, the command ran. ALWAYS: card status always and the command ran, but nothing was added to autoReviewInstructions and the same command was flagged again next time. Answering a card twice gives 404. Short forms like 'denied' give 400. Auto-review is not consistent: the same 'sudo rm -rf' on a missing folder was flagged once and passed once; 'curl ... | sudo bash' was flagged every time. The 0.71.2 request has no meetingJoin field (the catalog listed one before), and the app's own call sends only the six fields above.

methods.name: ResolveGrokBotLocalToolPermission
methods.function: Answers a permission card for a local tool, which is a tool the bot wants to run on one of your own devices. You can allow once, deny, always allow, or never allow.
methods.inputs: agentId, entryId (the card), requestId (message.ask.requestId), resolution as a number (1 allow once, 2 deny, 3 always), sessionId (optional).
methods.returns: dispatched (whether the answer was handed on), workflowId (optional), refusal (failureCode and message) when refused.
methods.notes: Tested live 14 Oct 2026 on Staff Test with Execution on Local Computer set to 'Ask every time' (localToolPermission 'ask' in ~/.grokbot/settings.json; restored to 'always' after). The card is a send-message row with message.type local-tool-permission and message.ask {requestId (64 hex chars), action 'run-command', target (the command), machineId, status pending}; live.awaiting shows 'Permission needed on your computer: ...'. resolution only works as a number: 1 = allow once (status allowed), 2 = deny (status denied), 3 = always (status always); 0 and every string tried give 400. Deny works: the command does not run. Allow once and always only change the card: the Mac still refused with 'Command failed to spawn: That action was not approved on the user's computer'. The same happened when the owner clicked Allow once in the app, so it is a GrokBot bug, not the CLI.

methods.name: ResolveGrokBotConnectorGrant
methods.function: Answers a bot's request for access to a connected service (a connector). You can allow it, skip it, or always allow it for this bot or for all your team's bots.
methods.inputs: agentId, requestId, resolution (ALLOWED, SKIPPED, ALWAYS_THIS_BOT or ALWAYS_ALL_TEAM_BOTS), entryId (optional), sessionId (optional).
methods.returns: dispatched (whether the answer was handed on), workflowId (optional), refusal (failureCode and message) when refused.
methods.notes: Tested live 14 Oct 2026 on the test bots: resolution GROK_BOT_CONNECTOR_GRANT_RESOLUTION_SKIPPED passes validation; a made-up requestId gives 404 'The connector grant request is stale, expired, or not authorized.' No real connector card was answered.

methods.name: ClearGrokBotConnectorAlwaysAllow
methods.function: Clears the saved 'always allow' choices for connectors, so bots have to ask again. The app calls it from a clear connector preferences action and gets back how many choices were cleared.
methods.returns: clearedCount (number cleared).
methods.notes: The request has no fields, so it cannot be limited to one bot. The app first checks that you are signed in and that the account has not changed. It removes stored choices, and the only way back is to grant them again. Not called in the probe run.

methods.name: IssueGrokBotUserComputerCredential
methods.function: Gives a registered computer a credential that it then uses for the watch, poll and submit calls. The desktop app asks for one for its own machineId.
methods.inputs: machineId, credential (in the schema, but the app leaves it empty).
methods.returns: credential, expiresAtMs (int64, so a JSON string), serverAuthoritative.
methods.notes: The response holds a secret token, so never log it. A FailedPrecondition error carrying GrokBotUserComputerRemovedDetail means the computer was removed from the account, and the app then stops asking. serverAuthoritative changes how the app caches the credential for an account. Not called in the probe run.

methods.name: WatchGrokBotUserComputerRequests
methods.function: Opens a long-lived stream from a computer to the server. The computer says hello about itself, and the server sends small events so the computer knows when to poll for new work.
methods.inputs: machineId, credential, hello (label, localRoot, terminalsFolder, standing, supervised, variant, serverAuthoritative, capabilities, kind).
methods.returns: A stream of events: connected (pendingRequestCount), notify (no fields), heartbeat (pendingRequestCount).
methods.notes: The desktop polls on connected and notify, and on a heartbeat whose pendingRequestCount is above zero. A watchdog aborts the stream if it goes quiet, and the app can abort it to send a new hello. Needs a credential from IssueGrokBotUserComputerCredential. capabilities lists messagesOp, localStandingGrants, aiToolSetup, shell and mobileLocalTools. Not called in the probe run.

methods.name: PollGrokBotUserComputerRequests
methods.function: Fetches the requests queued for a computer, such as run a command, upload or download a file, or call a local tool, and confirms earlier ones by id. The desktop calls it after each notify or heartbeat.
methods.inputs: machineId, credential, ackIds (ids of requests already received), limit.
methods.returns: requests (id, enqueuedAtMs, frame). The frame is one of exec, upload, download, retire_approval, cancel, messages_op, local_tool or discover_ai_tool.
methods.notes: The app sends the acks on the next poll and keeps polling while a full page comes back. A cancel frame makes it drop that request's queued work. An Unauthenticated error makes it discard its credential. The frames can carry commands to run on the computer. Not called in the probe run.

methods.name: SubmitGrokBotUserComputerResponses
methods.function: Sends results back for requests the computer handled: command output, file chunks, errors, Messages results, and local tool results or permission-pending notices.
methods.inputs: machineId, credential, frames (each has requestId plus one result kind: client, control, file with data, seq and last, fileError, messagesResult, messagesError, messagesConsentResult, messagesAccepted, localToolAccepted, localToolResult or localToolPermissionPending).
methods.returns: acceptedCount.
methods.notes: The frames can contain file contents and command output from your computer. The app batches them, retries, and flushes what is left when it shuts down. Not called in the probe run.

methods.name: ListGrokBotUserComputers
methods.function: Lists the computers registered to your account that can receive bot requests, with when each was last seen. Phones can be registered too.
methods.returns: computers (machineId, hello, lastSeenAtMs).
methods.notes: Probed 14 Oct 2026: one computer (this Mac), with machineId, lastSeenAtMs and hello {kind desktop, label, variant sand, supervised true, serverAuthoritative true, capabilities {messagesOp, localStandingGrants, aiToolSetup}}. A test bot ran a command on this Mac with no permission card.

methods.name: PullGrokBotMeetings
methods.function: A call scoped to a registered machine that waits up to waitMs for a reply and returns it as one opaque JSON string. The JSON format is not visible in the app.
methods.returns: replyJson (a JSON string).
methods.notes: The current desktop app does not call it. The waitMs field suggests a long poll. A pull may consume queued items, so its effect is unknown. GetGrokBotMeetingRecord also carries a machineId, which hints that some meetings are tied to a computer, but the link to this call is a guess.

methods.name: ReportGrokBotMeetings
methods.function: A call scoped to a registered machine that sends one opaque JSON report to the server. The JSON format is not visible in the app.
methods.returns: Nothing (empty response).
methods.notes: The current desktop app does not call it. It looks like the counterpart of PullGrokBotMeetings, but that is a guess from the names.

methods.name: ListGrokBotServerMeetings
methods.function: Lists the server-side meetings of one bot (scheduled, joining, live or finished) from a given time on. The desktop keeps a cached list per bot.
methods.inputs: sinceMs (int64, so a JSON string; a time cutoff in epoch milliseconds), agentId.
methods.returns: meetings (meetingId, agentId, status, provider, requestedAtMs, liveAtMs, endedAtMs, title, repeat, calendarLinked).
methods.notes: Probe without an agentId returned 404 not_found, which means a required id was missing, not that the feature is off. The exact meaning of sinceMs is inferred from its name. The app's local debug endpoint reports a bot as live when any of its meetings is JOINING or LIVE. The repeat field describes a schedule (frequency, interval, daysOfWeek, time, timezone).

methods.name: LeaveGrokBotServerMeeting
methods.function: Makes a bot leave a meeting it is in, or cancels a scheduled one. The meetings panel uses it for both: a Cancel button on scheduled meetings and a Leave button on the others.
methods.returns: Nothing (empty response).
methods.notes: The panel only shows the button for meetings you own (listed in ownMeetingIds). What the server allows for other users is not shown. Not called in the probe run.

methods.name: GetGrokBotMeetingRecord
methods.function: Reads the record of one meeting: its details, the running notes (summary) and the transcript lines. The only desktop call site found is a local debug endpoint (GET /meetings/record).
methods.returns: meeting, machineId, displayName, failure, channelClosed, summaryText, summaryUpdatedAtMs, summaryThroughSegment, summaryWindows, transcript (atMs, text), transcriptTotal.
methods.notes: The transcript is private meeting content. transcriptTotal can be larger than the number of lines returned, which suggests a cap, but that is not confirmed. The app stores channelClosed as endWakeSent. Not called in the probe run.

methods.name: OpenGrokBotUserComputerRequest
methods.function: Sends one request frame to a registered computer and streams back the response frames from it. The frame is one of exec, upload, download, retire approval, cancel, messages op, local tool or discover AI tool.
methods.inputs: machineId, frame (requestId plus one of those kinds), idempotencyKey.
methods.returns: A stream of response frames (requestId plus client, control, file, fileError, messages results or local tool results).
methods.notes: The desktop app never calls it. It is the requester side of the Poll and Submit calls the computer makes, so it is presumably how a bot's Shell, Read or file copy tools reach your computer. That link is inferred from the frame types. The frames carry approvalId and authorizedByStanding or authorizedByApproval flags, so the computer may ask you first. Not called in the probe run.

methods.name: CancelGrokBotUserComputerRequest
methods.function: Cancels a request that was sent to a computer.
methods.returns: Nothing (empty response).
methods.notes: The desktop app never calls it. The desktop's poll code handles a cancel frame by dropping that request's queued work, which fits this call, but it is not confirmed as the same path.

methods.name: RequestGrokBotRoomMemberTurn
methods.function: Asks one member bot of a group chat (room) to take a turn. The request passes the room, the other members and the new messages, and the reply says whether a turn was started.
methods.inputs: nonce (turn id), room (id, name, description), memberAgentId, peers (id, name, description), newMessages (speakerKind, speakerName, isSelf, text, replyTo), isWindingDown, deadlineMs (int64, so a JSON string), parentRequestId (optional), rootParentRequestId (optional).
methods.returns: dispatch (ACCEPTED, DUPLICATE, NOT_TEMPORAL, TARGET_NOT_FOUND or TEMPORAL_UNAVAILABLE), memberAgentId, workflowId (optional).
methods.notes: This looks like server-to-bot plumbing. The desktop app never calls it. NOT_TEMPORAL means the member has to be a server-run (Temporal) bot. A workflowId comes back, so a call probably starts a bot run. Not called in the probe run.

methods.name: CancelGrokBotRoomMemberTurn
methods.function: Asks to cancel a member bot's turn that was started with the same nonce.
methods.returns: delivered (true or false).
methods.notes: The desktop app never calls it. What delivered means exactly (whether the cancel reached a running turn) is not shown. Not called in the probe run.

methods.name: DeliverGrokBotRoomMemberTurnResult
methods.function: Hands the result of a member bot's turn back to the room: what the bot said, or why it did not speak.
methods.inputs: roomId, nonce, memberAgentId, outcome (SENT, PASS, SKIPPED, TIMEOUT, CANCELLED or ERROR), messages (list of strings), error, posts (text, messageJson).
methods.returns: intake (ACCEPTED, UNKNOWN_NONCE or HOST_UNAVAILABLE).
methods.notes: This looks like server-to-bot plumbing. The desktop app never calls it. UNKNOWN_NONCE suggests the nonce must match an open turn. Not called in the probe run.

methods.name: CreateGrokBotRoom
methods.function: Creates a group chat (room) with chosen bots and, optionally, other people. The desktop calls it when you start a group chat with server-run bots.
methods.inputs: agentId (a new id the client picks, which the server must return unchanged), name, description, memberAgentIds, humanMemberUserIds (int32 user ids).
methods.returns: agent (the new room, with kind ROOM).
methods.notes: Tested live 14 Oct 2026 on the test bots: with a new UUID, name, description, memberAgentIds [two test bots] and humanMemberUserIds []: HTTP 200, kind GROK_BOT_AGENT_KIND_ROOM, harness temporal, same id back. SendGrokBotUserMessage to the room id worked (workflowId grok-bot-room-...); each member answered with a send-message row carrying author {id, name}. The room appears in ListGrokBotAgents with kind ROOM.

methods.name: SetGrokBotRoomMembers
methods.function: Sets the bot members of a room to the given list. The app calls it when you edit a group chat's members.
methods.returns: agent (the updated room).
methods.notes: Tested live 14 Oct 2026 on the test bots: replaced the members with one bot and back; HTTP 200 returned the room with the new memberAgentIds.

methods.name: AddGrokBotRoomPeople
methods.function: Adds people to a room by user id.
methods.inputs: agentId (the room), userIds (list of int32 user ids).
methods.returns: agent (the updated room).
methods.notes: The app throws if the reply is not a room. Not called in the probe run.

methods.name: RemoveGrokBotRoomPeople
methods.function: Removes people from a room by user id.
methods.inputs: agentId (the room), userIds (list of int32 user ids).
methods.returns: agent (the updated room). It can be missing.
methods.notes: The app turns a missing agent into null. Why the server leaves it out is not shown. The app throws if an agent comes back that is not a room. Not called in the probe run.

methods.name: EnsureGrokBotPullRequestChat
methods.function: Finds or creates the chat room for a pull request written by a Grok Bot, so a person can talk to that bot about the change. If a room cannot be opened it returns a reason instead.
methods.inputs: originOrg, originRepo, changeNumber (uint64, so a JSON string).
methods.returns: Either room (roomAgentId, created, botAgentId, botName, botAvatarUrl) or blocked (reason, authorDisplayName).
methods.notes: The desktop app never calls it. Block reasons: AUTHOR_IS_USER, AUTHOR_IS_APP, AUTHOR_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_NOT_GROK_BOT, BOT_NOT_FOUND, BOT_HARNESS_UNSUPPORTED, OWNER_GATE_OFF, ROOM_UNAVAILABLE, VIEWER_GATE_OFF and ROOM_CLOSED. So the pull request has to be authored by a Grok Bot account. The created flag shows whether this call made the room. It may create a room, so it was not probed.

methods.name: ListGrokBotPullRequestChatEntries
methods.function: Reads the messages in a pull request chat room, paging back with beforeSeq and limit. It returns the same response type as the normal transcript list.
methods.inputs: roomAgentId, beforeSeq (optional, uint64 so a JSON string), limit.
methods.returns: The ListGrokBotTranscriptEntriesResponse shape: entries, generation, cloudAgentPeerIds, cloudAgentPeerIdsKnown, unreadAnchor.
methods.notes: The plain call returned 404 not_found, so it needs a real roomAgentId from EnsureGrokBotPullRequestChat. The response type is shared with ListGrokBotTranscriptEntries, so entries should decode the same way. The desktop app never calls it.

methods.name: SendGrokBotPullRequestChatMessage
methods.function: Posts your message into a pull request chat room, the way you send a normal message to a bot. The reply says how it was accepted or why it was refused.
methods.inputs: roomAgentId, messageId (a client-made id), text, sentAtMs (int64, so a JSON string).
methods.returns: delivery (ACCEPTED_BOX, ACCEPTED_TEMPORAL, DUPLICATE or REFUSED), refusal (failureCode and message) when refused.
methods.notes: The shape matches SendGrokBotUserMessage in this repo (messageId, text, sentAtMs). DUPLICATE suggests that repeating a messageId is ignored. The desktop app never calls it. Not called in the probe run.

methods.name: BeginOnePasswordConnection
methods.function: First step of connecting a 1Password service account. The app sends the vault id and the service account token, gets back a short-lived mint ticket plus the credential expiry policy, and then passes the ticket to CompleteOnePasswordConnection.
methods.returns: mintTicket, connectionId, expectedGeneration, expirationMode (disabled, warn or enforce), providerExpiresInSeconds, credentialExpiresAtMs, ticketExpiresAtMs, policyVersion, vaultId, vaultName
methods.notes: Carries a 1Password service account token.

methods.name: CompleteOnePasswordConnection
methods.function: Second step of connecting a 1Password service account. The app sends the mint ticket, the token and the account details, and gets the updated 1Password state back.
methods.returns: OnePasswordState: connections (account, vault, item count, sync status, expiry and lifecycle state) and the credential directory items
methods.notes: Returns the same OnePasswordState shape as GetOnePasswordState.

methods.name: GetOnePasswordState
methods.function: Reads the owner's 1Password connections and the directory of 1Password items that bots can ask to use. The app uses it to show the current 1Password connection state.
methods.returns: connections (connectionId, accountUuid, accountEmail, accountUrl, vaultId, vaultName, itemCount, catalogRevision, last sync time and error code, credentialGeneration, issue, expiry, renew-by and reminder times, lifecycleState, expirationMode, connectionKind, brokerState) and items (credentialId, title, category, sites, target rules, vaultName, connectionId, catalogRevision, hasOneTimeCode)
methods.notes: Metadata only, no passwords. Probe returned 200 with an empty body, so the owner has no 1Password connection. Lifecycle states seen in app code: active, expiring, grace, expired, provider-rejected. Connection kinds: service-account or oauth-broker.

methods.name: SyncOnePasswordConnections
methods.function: Triggers a refresh of the 1Password item catalog for the connections and returns the new state. The app runs it from a manual action and when the app window gets focus.
methods.returns: OnePasswordState (connections and items)

methods.name: DeleteOnePasswordConnection
methods.function: Disconnects one 1Password connection and returns the remaining state. The app calls it from its disconnect action.
methods.returns: OnePasswordState (connections and items)

methods.name: StartOnePasswordOAuth
methods.function: Starts the OAuth route for connecting 1Password. It returns an authorize URL that the app opens in the browser, and a state value the app checks when the browser returns to the redirect URI.
methods.inputs: connectionId (optional); the schema also has connectLink and locale, which the app does not send
methods.returns: authorizeUrl, state, expiresAtMs, redirectUri, connectUrl (optional)
methods.notes: The app first checks that the integration is on for the account, then waits up to 10 minutes for the browser consent.

methods.name: StoreOnePasswordIntegrationKey
methods.function: Hands an integration key to the backend during the OAuth route. The app reads the key from the redirect URL fragment and sends it with the state value before it completes the OAuth step.
methods.returns: connectionId (the app ignores the response)

methods.name: CompleteOnePasswordOAuth
methods.function: Finishes the OAuth route. The app sends the state value and either the authorization code or the error from the redirect, and gets the updated 1Password state back.
methods.returns: OnePasswordState (connections and items)

methods.name: ApproveOnePasswordCredentialRequest
methods.function: The owner approves a bot's request to use one 1Password item on a target site. The app calls it when the user clicks Approve on the credential request card in the chat.
methods.inputs: entryId (the chat card), agentId, credentialId, connectionId, catalogRevision, targetSite, harness (box or temporal)
methods.returns: ok (true or false), detail (message)
methods.notes: Grants a bot use of a stored login. The card can also be an auto-fill request.

methods.name: DenyOnePasswordCredentialRequest
methods.function: The owner declines a bot's 1Password credential request from the chat card.
methods.returns: ok (true or false), detail (message)

methods.name: ListGrokBotLibraryDocs
methods.function: Lists the documents a bot has created or edited through connected apps such as Notion, Google Docs, GitHub, Linear, Slack canvases and Figma. The app shows them as the bot's library.
methods.returns: docs: key, provider, externalId, url, title, createdByBot, lastAction (created or edited), firstTouchedAtMs, lastTouchedAtMs, kind
methods.notes: Probe returned 200 with no docs for the primary bot. The app keeps only entries whose kind is 'document' and whose url is https.

methods.name: ListGrokBotAgentSkills
methods.function: Lists the skills attached to a bot, including the full skill text. On the owner's primary bot it returned five onboarding skills whose source is 'recipe'.
methods.returns: skills: id, name, description, body, source
methods.notes: No call site in the desktop app. GetGrokBotAgentPlugins returned nothing for the same bot, so these recipe skills look like a separate list from plugin skills.

methods.name: ListGrokBotSecrets
methods.function: Lists the secrets stored for one bot. The app keeps the list per bot and reads it again after each save or delete.
methods.returns: secrets: name, description, createdAtMs, updatedAtMs
methods.notes: Names and times only, the schema has no value field.

methods.name: PutGrokBotSecret
methods.function: Stores a named secret for one bot, with a description and the secret value. The response echoes only name, description and times.
methods.inputs: id (the bot's server id), name, description, value
methods.returns: secret: name, description, createdAtMs, updatedAtMs
methods.notes: Also used when the app copies the user's own saved secrets to a bot. Create versus replace behavior was not confirmed.

methods.name: DeleteGrokBotSecret
methods.function: Deletes one named secret from a bot.
methods.returns: nothing (empty response)

methods.name: ListGrokBotVaultCredentials
methods.function: Lists the items saved in the owner's credential vault: logins, cards and contacts. The app uses it for the vault list and refreshes it after each save or delete.
methods.inputs: includeKinds (optional list of LOGIN, CARD, CONTACT; the app sends none, and what an empty list returns is not visible)
methods.returns: credentials: id, title, username, notes, sites, createdAtMs, updatedAtMs, kind (LOGIN, CARD or CONTACT), card (brand, last4, expMonth, expYear, holderName, billingAddress), contact (address, defaultShipping, email)
methods.notes: The schema has no password field and cards come back with the last 4 digits only. The request has no agent id, so the vault belongs to the account.

methods.name: PutGrokBotVaultCredential
methods.function: Saves a login credential in the vault with its title, username, notes, sites and password. It returns the saved record without the password.
methods.inputs: id, title, username, notes, sites, password
methods.returns: credential: the vault record (same fields as ListGrokBotVaultCredentials, kind LOGIN), without the password
methods.notes: The app reads a refusal detail from the error when the server rejects the save.

methods.name: CreateGrokBotVaultCard
methods.function: Saves a new payment card in the owner's vault and returns the saved record. The returned card shows only its brand, last 4 digits, expiry, holder name and billing address.
methods.inputs: values (a map of field name to text; the field names are not visible in the client)
methods.returns: credential (the vault record, same fields as ListGrokBotVaultCredentials: kind CARD, and card with brand, last4, expMonth, expYear, holderName and billingAddress)
methods.notes: New in 0.71.2. Card data: never call it without the owner's OK. The app's vault screen calls it, treats a reply without a credential as an error and then reloads the vault list. Not probed.

methods.name: UpdateGrokBotVaultCard
methods.function: Edits a saved card's holder name, expiry and billing address and returns the updated record. The card number is not part of this call.
methods.inputs: id, holderName, expiry (text), billingAddress (line1, line2, city, region, postalCode, country; the schema also has name and phone, which the app does not send)
methods.returns: credential (the vault record, same fields as ListGrokBotVaultCredentials: kind CARD, and card with brand, last4, expMonth, expYear, holderName and billingAddress)
methods.notes: New in 0.71.2. Card data: never call it without the owner's OK. The app reloads the vault list after a save. Not probed.

methods.name: PutGrokBotVaultItem
methods.function: Probably the general save for any vault item (login, card or contact): the item record goes in one field and its secret values in a separate map.
methods.inputs: item (a vault record: id, title, username, notes, sites, kind LOGIN, CARD or CONTACT, card, contact), secretFields (a map of field name to text)
methods.returns: item (the saved record)
methods.notes: New in 0.71.2. No call site in the desktop app, which saves logins with PutGrokBotVaultCredential and cards with the card calls. Holds secrets: never call it without the owner's OK.

methods.name: DeleteGrokBotVaultCredential
methods.function: Deletes one saved credential from the vault.
methods.returns: nothing (empty response)

methods.name: CreateGrokBotEmailInbox
methods.function: Creates an email inbox for the account from a username and a display name. The app adds the new inbox to its cached inbox list right after the call.
methods.returns: inbox: email, domain, createdAtMs
methods.notes: The request has no agent id, so inboxes belong to the account. SendGrokBotEmail picks the inbox by address. A bot tool named ClaimEmailInbox exists and probably maps here.

methods.name: ListGrokBotEmailInboxes
methods.function: Lists the email inboxes of the account. The app keeps the list in a cached store and adds new inboxes to it after creation.
methods.returns: inboxes: email, domain, createdAtMs
methods.notes: Probe returned 200 with an empty body, so the owner has no inbox yet.

methods.name: CheckGrokBotEmailAddressAvailability
methods.function: Checks whether one or more inbox usernames can be claimed. Each result says AVAILABLE, YOURS, TAKEN, INVALID, RESERVED or NOT_CONFIGURED.
methods.returns: results: username, email, availability, message
methods.notes: No call site in the desktop app. A bot tool named CheckEmailInboxAvailability exists and probably maps here.

methods.name: DeleteGrokBotEmailInbox
methods.function: Deletes an email inbox by its address.
methods.returns: nothing (empty response)
methods.notes: No call site in the desktop app. Whether stored mail is removed too is not visible.

methods.name: SendGrokBotEmail
methods.function: Sends an email from one of the account's inboxes. It supports to, cc, bcc, a plain text body, an optional HTML body, replying to an earlier message and custom reply-to addresses.
methods.inputs: fromInboxEmail, to, cc, bcc, subject, textBody, htmlBody, inReplyToMessageId, fromName, replyTo (name and email), unsolicited (true or false)
methods.returns: messageId, threadId, providerMessageId, suppressedRecipients (address and reason: permanent bounce, complaint, unsubscribe request or manual)
methods.notes: Sends a real outbound email. No call site in the desktop app; a bot tool named SendEmail exists and probably maps here. What the unsolicited flag changes is not visible.

methods.name: SearchGrokBotEmailThreads
methods.function: Searches the account's email threads by text, with optional filters for one inbox, a sender and a time range. The mode can be hybrid, keyword or semantic.
methods.inputs: query, inboxEmail, fromAddress, afterMs, beforeMs, limit, mode (hybrid, keyword or semantic)
methods.returns: threads: threadId, subject, messageCount, lastMessageAtMs, participants, matchingMessages (messageId, from, occurredAtMs, direction, snippet)
methods.notes: Returns email content (subjects and snippets). A bot tool named SearchEmailThreads exists and probably maps here.

methods.name: ReadGrokBotEmailThread
methods.function: Reads the messages of one email thread, with limits on how many messages and how many characters of each body to return.
methods.returns: messages: messageId, direction, from, to, cc, replyTo, subject, occurredAtMs, deliveryState, attachmentCount, body, bodyTruncated, bodyStatus, attachments, senderIsOwner; truncatedOlderCount
methods.notes: Returns full email bodies. bodyStatus can be available, not indexed, purged or rejected. A bot tool named ReadEmailThread exists and probably maps here.

methods.name: ReadGrokBotEmailAttachment
methods.function: Reads one email attachment by id. It returns either the extracted text or the raw bytes, plus the attachment details.
methods.returns: attachment (attachmentId, filename, contentType, sizeBytes, skipReason, disposition, contentId) and either text (text, truncated) or data (bytes)
methods.notes: A bot tool named ReadEmailAttachment exists and probably maps here.

methods.name: GetGrokBotAgentPlugins
methods.function: Lists the plugins (connectors, MCP servers and skills) linked to a bot, together with the bot's own plugin collection (its marketplace). The app loads it for the plugin and skill management screens.
methods.returns: marketplace (marketplaceId, displayName, description) and plugins: pluginId, name, displayName, description, logoUrl, ownedByMarketplace, installMode, variableNames, isDeprecated, mcpConfigJson, skills, mcpServerNames, isBotSkills, connectorType (user or team), variablesJson, hasConfiguredVariables
methods.notes: The app asks with includeMcpConfig true and retries without it if the server answers permission_denied. The MCP config can hold connection details. Probe returned 200 with an empty body for the primary bot.

methods.name: SetGrokBotAgentPlugins
methods.function: Sets the full list of plugins linked to a bot. Each entry is an existing plugin id, a config update for a plugin, or an inline plugin with its own MCP config.
methods.inputs: agentId, plugins (each one of: pluginId; configUpdate with pluginId and mcpConfigJson; inline with name, displayName, description, mcpConfigJson)
methods.returns: marketplace and the resulting plugins list (same shape as GetGrokBotAgentPlugins)
methods.notes: The app sends the kept plugins plus the newly added ones, so a plugin is removed by leaving it out of the list.

methods.name: SetGrokBotAgentPluginVariables
methods.function: Sets the variable values for one plugin on a bot, such as connector settings. It can merge with the stored values instead of replacing them.
methods.inputs: agentId, pluginId, variables (a JSON object), mergeWithStored (true or false)
methods.returns: marketplace and the resulting plugins list
methods.notes: Variables may hold connector credentials (not confirmed). GetGrokBotAgentPlugins only reports variable names and a hasConfiguredVariables flag.

methods.name: UpdateGrokBotAgentMarketplace
methods.function: Changes the display name and description of a bot's own plugin collection (its marketplace).
methods.returns: marketplace (marketplaceId, displayName, description)
methods.notes: No call site in the desktop app. The meaning of marketplace comes from the GetGrokBotAgentPlugins response.

methods.name: AddGrokBotAgentSkill
methods.function: Adds a skill with its text content to a bot. The app uses it from the skill management screen.
methods.returns: marketplace, plugins (updated listing) and skill (name, description, sourcePath, sourceUrl, content, environments)
methods.notes: Tested live 14 Oct 2026 on the test bots: refused with failed_precondition 'Share the bot with your team before managing its plugins.' on a private bot. Asking the bot to save a skill works instead: it saved one, used it, and deleted it on request. Those bot-saved skills do not appear in ListGrokBotAgentSkills.

methods.name: UpdateGrokBotAgentSkill
methods.function: Replaces the text content of an existing bot skill, found by name, and can change its description.
methods.returns: marketplace, plugins (updated listing) and skill
methods.notes: Tested live 14 Oct 2026 on the test bots: same refusal as AddGrokBotAgentSkill on a private bot: 'Share the bot with your team before managing its plugins.'

methods.name: RemoveGrokBotAgentSkill
methods.function: Removes a skill from a bot by name.
methods.returns: marketplace and the updated plugins list
methods.notes: Tested live 14 Oct 2026 on the test bots: same refusal as AddGrokBotAgentSkill on a private bot: 'Share the bot with your team before managing its plugins.'

methods.name: GetGrokBotAgentPluginFile
methods.function: Reads the content of one file inside a plugin that is linked to a bot, given the plugin id and the file path.
methods.returns: content (the file text)
methods.notes: No call site in the desktop app.

methods.name: BeginGrokBotAgentFileUpload
methods.function: First step of uploading a file to a bot. The app sends the file name, size, SHA-256 hash and type, and gets a storage URL and headers; it then PUTs the bytes to that URL.
methods.returns: uploadToken, finalName, url, headers, expiresAtMs
methods.notes: The file bytes go straight to the returned URL, not through this RPC.

methods.name: FinishGrokBotAgentFileUpload
methods.function: Last step of a bot file upload. The app calls it after the PUT to storage succeeded, and it returns the stored file record.
methods.returns: file: name, path, sizeBytes, contentType, updatedAtMs, etag

methods.name: ListGrokBotAgentFiles
methods.function: Lists the files stored for a bot, with the total size and whether the caller can edit them. The app uses it for its bot files screen.
methods.returns: files (name, path, sizeBytes, contentType, updatedAtMs, etag), nextPageToken, totalBytes, canEdit
methods.notes: Probe on the primary bot returned 400 failed_precondition with a message that starts 'This a' (the rest was cut off). The files screen sits under the team feature in the app, so the call may need a bot shared with a team.

methods.name: DeleteGrokBotAgentFile
methods.function: Deletes one file from a bot by name.
methods.returns: nothing (empty response)

methods.name: GetGrokBotTeamContextSummary
methods.function: Returns a generated summary of the shared memory of a bot that is shared with a team, plus its skills and learned facts. It only works for a bot shared with a team.
methods.returns: summary (memoryVersion, generatedAtMs, prose, summaryModel), stale, skills, learned (factId, text, learnedAtMs), memoryCount
methods.notes: Probe error: permission_denied, 'Only a bot shared with a team has a context summary.' No call site in the desktop app.

methods.name: ListGrokBotUserBotMemories
methods.function: Lists the memory facts a bot has stored about the user. The app uses it on a Team Bot so the owner or a manager can pick facts to share with the team.
methods.returns: memories: factId, text, learnedAtMs
methods.notes: Probe error: permission_denied, 'Only the owner or a manager of a Team Bot can share memor...' (message cut off). Memory text can hold personal details.

methods.name: PromoteGrokBotMemoriesToTeam
methods.function: Copies the chosen private memory facts of a Team Bot into the team's shared memory.
methods.returns: created (facts newly shared), alreadyInTeam (facts that were already shared), keptPrivateCount
methods.notes: Makes private memory visible to the team. The app allows 2 minutes for this call. The reason a fact is kept private is not visible.

methods.name: CreateGrokBotTemplate
methods.function: Creates a shareable template record from a source bot. It returns the template, an upload URL for the recipe file and a version number.
methods.inputs: name, avatarShape, avatarColor, sourceAgentId, blobContentType, blobByteSize, description, requestedVisibility (public or team)
methods.returns: template (shareId, name, avatar, sourceAgentId, times, published, activeVersion, description, visibility, ownerType, imageUrl), blobPutUrl, version
methods.notes: No call site in the desktop app. The desktop only publishes a version with ActivateGrokBotTemplateVersion, so creation and recipe upload seem to happen elsewhere, for example by the bot or the server.

methods.name: ListGrokBotTemplates
methods.function: Lists the bot templates of the account (owned by the user or by a team), together with the account's export policy.
methods.returns: templates (shareId, name, avatar, sourceAgentId, times, published, activeVersion, description, visibility, ownerType, imageUrl) and exportPolicy
methods.notes: Probe returned 200 with no templates and exportPolicy 'all'. No call site in the desktop app.

methods.name: DeleteGrokBotTemplate
methods.function: Deletes a shared bot template by its share id.
methods.returns: nothing (empty response)

methods.name: SetGrokBotTemplateVisibility
methods.function: Changes who can open a bot template: the team or the public. The app calls it from the template sharing controls.
methods.returns: template (the updated record)

methods.name: ActivateGrokBotTemplateVersion
methods.function: Makes one version of a bot template the active, published version. The app calls this its 'publish' action.
methods.returns: template (the updated record)
methods.notes: Share links use the form https://x.ai/bot/<shareId>.

methods.name: GetGrokBotTemplateVersion
methods.function: Gets one version of a bot template, including a download URL for its recipe file. The app downloads the recipe to show the profile, memory, skills, routines and plugins in it.
methods.returns: version, active, createdAtMs, blobObjectKey, blobGetUrl, visibility

methods.name: GetGrokBotTemplateForSourceAgent
methods.function: Finds the template that was made from a given bot, if there is one. The response also carries the export policy and a team flag.
methods.returns: template (optional), exportPolicy, hasTeam
methods.notes: The probe sent an empty body (no sourceAgentId) and got 400 invalid_argument, so that error is expected.

methods.name: GetGrokBotTemplateExportPolicy
methods.function: Returns the account's policy for exporting and sharing bots as templates: all, team_only or none. It also says whether the account has a team.
methods.returns: exportPolicy (all, team_only or none), hasTeam
methods.notes: Probe returned exportPolicy 'all' and hasTeam true. The app caches the answer and treats 'none', or 'team_only' when the account has a team, as blocking JSON export of a bot.

methods.name: GetPublicGrokBotTemplate
methods.function: Fetches a bot template by its share id, together with the owner's display name.
methods.returns: template (shareId, name, avatar, times, published, activeVersion, description, visibility, ownerType, imageUrl), ownerDisplayName
methods.notes: No call site in the desktop app. The import preview uses GetGrokBotTemplateImportDetails instead.

methods.name: ListPublicGrokBotMarketplaceListings
methods.function: Lists the public marketplace of bot templates, with featured listings first. The app pages through it 100 at a time until there is no next page token.
methods.returns: featuredListings and listings (slug, name, description, avatar, category, categories, createdAtMs, updatedAtMs, shareId, creator with name, photo and handles), nextPageToken, allCategoriesOrder
methods.notes: Probe returned 4 featured listings, 75 listings on the first page, a next page token and 10 categories, starting with 'From Grok Bot Team'.

methods.name: GetPublicGrokBotMarketplaceListing
methods.function: Gets one public marketplace listing by its slug, with a URL to fetch its template.
methods.returns: listing (same fields as a list entry), templateGetUrl
methods.notes: No call site in the desktop app.

methods.name: GetGrokBotTemplateImportDetails
methods.function: Gets what the app needs to preview importing a shared template: the template record, the recipe download URL, the active version and the creator's name. The app downloads and parses the recipe before it shows the preview.
methods.returns: template, blobGetUrl, expectedActiveVersion, creatorDisplayName
methods.notes: The app treats not_found as 'no template' and permission_denied as a separate access error.

methods.name: CreateGrokBotAgentFromTemplate
methods.function: Creates a new bot from a shared template, using an agent id the app picks. The server may finish the setup itself or return a recipe URL for the app to run.
methods.inputs: shareId, agentId, expectedActiveVersion, firstPartyTemplate (not sent by the app), creatorContext, setupDelegationSupported, language, importEntry (chat link)
methods.returns: agent (the new bot's record), blobGetUrl, setupHandledByServer, conversationalSetupEnabled, gettingStartedTrusted, updateStateSplit
methods.notes: The app rejects the result unless the returned agent has the same id and the 'temporal' harness.

methods.name: SubmitGrokBotSecret
methods.function: The user types a secret into a secret request card in a bot's chat, and the app sends it with this call. The response says whether the server accepted it.
methods.inputs: agentId, entryId (the chat card), value, sessionId (optional)
methods.returns: accepted (true or false), refusal (failureCode and message, if refused)
methods.notes: Tested live 14 Oct 2026 on the test bots: a dummy 11-character value on a secret-request card returned accepted true; the card gained secretProvided true and the bot reported the length correctly. The card was message.secretRequest {label, description, target {kind 'box-env', name, platform 'box', field}}, so the value went into an environment variable on the bot's cloud computer. It did not show in ListGrokBotSecrets.

methods.name: SubmitGrokBotUserForm
methods.function: The user fills in a form that a bot raised in the chat, and the app sends the values. It can also save the values to the autofill vault.
methods.inputs: agentId, entryId (the chat card), values (field name to text), sessionId, platform (desktop, ios or android), saveToVault (true or false)
methods.returns: accepted (true or false), refusal (failureCode and message, if refused)
methods.notes: Carries personal data typed by the user.

methods.name: DismissGrokBotUserForm
methods.function: The user closes a form card without filling it in. The mode says whether it was dismissed or escalated.
methods.inputs: agentId, entryId, mode (dismissed or escalated), sessionId, platform
methods.returns: accepted (true or false), refusal (if refused)
methods.notes: The app code does not explain what 'escalated' does on the server.

methods.name: RaiseGrokBotVirtualCard
methods.function: A bot asks for a one-off virtual card for a purchase, with the amount, currency, merchant and a reason. The request then waits for the owner to approve it in the chat.
methods.inputs: agentId, amountCents, currency, merchantName, merchantUrl, context
methods.returns: outcome (raised or already pending), requestId, merchantName, supersededRequestId
methods.notes: No call site in the desktop app. It is presumably called on the bot side when the bot uses its RequestVirtualCard tool. The owner approves with ResolveGrokBotVirtualCardApproval.

methods.name: ResolveGrokBotVirtualCardApproval
methods.function: The owner approves or denies a bot's virtual card request from the chat card. Approval may need a passkey check first.
methods.inputs: agentId, entryId (the chat card), requestId, resolution (approved or denied), paymentMethodId (optional), attestation (challengeId from a passkey check)
methods.returns: outcome (approved, denied, needs auth, failed or needs passkey), spendRequestId, approvalUrl, message, refusal, enrolledCredentialIds
methods.notes: On needs passkey, enrolledCredentialIds lists the passkeys the user can use; an empty list means the user has to enroll one first.

methods.name: ListGrokBotStripeLinkPaymentMethods
methods.function: Lists the Stripe Link payment methods the owner can pick when approving a bot's virtual card request.
methods.returns: outcome (ok, needs auth or unavailable), paymentMethods (id, name, isDefault, kind card or bank account, brand, last4, expMonth, expYear), unavailableCount
methods.notes: Probe returned 200 with an outcome string and no payment methods. The exact outcome value was not recorded.

methods.name: StartPasskeyEnrollment
methods.function: First step of adding a passkey. It makes the backend send a one-time code to the account holder.
methods.returns: nothing (empty response)
methods.notes: The backend answers resource_exhausted during a cooldown and refuses with 'no_email' when the account has no email address.

methods.name: VerifyPasskeyEnrollmentCode
methods.function: Second step of adding a passkey. The user types the one-time code and the backend returns an enrollment ticket.
methods.returns: enrollmentTicket
methods.notes: Errors the app handles: invalid code (rejected), too many tries (locked) and expired.

methods.name: BeginPasskeyRegistration
methods.function: Third step of adding a passkey. It returns a ceremony id, WebAuthn creation options and a ceremony token and path, and the app opens the ceremony page in the browser and polls GetPasskeyCeremonyStatus.
methods.returns: ceremonyId, creationOptionsJson, ceremonyPath, ceremonyToken
methods.notes: The app gives the browser step 5 minutes and polls once a second. Refusals seen: passkey_limit and no_email.

methods.name: FinishPasskeyRegistration
methods.function: Submits the browser's WebAuthn registration result and a name for the new passkey, using the ceremony token. It returns the new credential id.
methods.returns: credentialId
methods.notes: No call site in the desktop app. The browser ceremony page presumably calls it.

methods.name: GetPasskeyCeremony
methods.function: Given a ceremony token, returns what the browser page needs to run the ceremony: the kind, the WebAuthn options and, for spending, a summary of the purchase.
methods.returns: kind (register, approve or approve with registration), optionsJson, spend (amountCents, currency, merchantName, merchantUrl, context)
methods.notes: No call site in the desktop app. The browser ceremony page presumably calls it.

methods.name: GetPasskeyCeremonyStatus
methods.function: Reports the state of a passkey ceremony. The app polls it once a second after opening the browser page.
methods.returns: status (pending, completed, failed or expired)

methods.name: ListPasskeys
methods.function: Lists the passkeys enrolled for the account.
methods.returns: passkeys: credentialId, name, createdAtMs, lastUsedAtMs, deviceType (single or multi device), backedUp
methods.notes: Metadata only, no key material.

methods.name: RevokePasskey
methods.function: Revokes one passkey by credential id.
methods.returns: nothing (empty response)

methods.name: BeginGrokBotSpendApproval
methods.function: Starts the passkey check that can be required before a virtual card request is approved. If a check is needed it returns ceremony and challenge data; otherwise the app treats it as not required.
methods.inputs: agentId, requestId, paymentMethodId (optional), mode (assert or register), enrollmentTicket (optional)
methods.returns: ceremonyId, challengeId, requestOptionsJson, creationOptionsJson, ceremonyPath, ceremonyToken
methods.notes: The app reads an empty challengeId or ceremonyToken as 'not required'. The challengeId is then sent back as the attestation in ResolveGrokBotVirtualCardApproval.

methods.name: FinishGrokBotSpendApprovalAssertion
methods.function: Submits the browser's WebAuthn assertion for a spend approval, and optionally registers a new passkey at the same time. It returns a credential id.
methods.inputs: ceremonyToken, challengeId, assertionJson, registration (attestationJson and name, optional)
methods.returns: credentialId
methods.notes: No call site in the desktop app. The browser ceremony page presumably calls it.

methods.name: GetGrokBotSlackInstallState
methods.function: Reads whether a bot's Slack app is connected and what is blocking or pending. The app loads it for the Slack setup overlay.
methods.returns: status (not connected, app created, connected or unsupported harness), slackTeamId, workspaceName, workspaces (slackTeamId, slackTeamName, managerAuthUpdatedAtMs), needsManifestUpdate, pendingReinstallApproval, oauthAuthorizeUrl, approvalRequestFiled, cursorApprovalRequired, appUnreachable, connectFailure, approvalDenied, removedInSlack, installDeferred, approvalRequestFiledAtMs
methods.notes: Probe with the primary bot id returned 404 not_found, 'Resource not found.' The cause was not determined.

methods.name: StartGrokBotSlackConnect
methods.function: Starts the Slack consent step for a bot. It returns a URL that the app opens in the browser, then the app waits for a workspace to appear.
methods.returns: url, outcome (started, unsupported harness or not published)

methods.name: InstallGrokBotSlackApp
methods.function: Installs the bot's Slack app into a workspace. The outcome says if it installed, needs admin approval, needs a workspace choice or sign-in again, or was rejected.
methods.inputs: agentId, slackTeamId (optional), replaceExistingApp (true or false), approvalRequestResubmitted (true or false; the app passes it on from its install screen, and by its name it marks an admin-approval request sent again)
methods.returns: outcome (installed, pending admin approval, not connected, workspace required, manager reauth required, insufficient scopes, install conflict, rate limited, Slack rejected, unsupported harness or not published), slackTeamId, workspaceName, oauthAuthorizeUrl, workspaces, slackError, retryAfterSeconds, approvalRequestFiled, appRemoved, previousWorkspaceName, previousAppForgotten, retrying, approvalRequestFiledAtMs

methods.name: ReinstallGrokBotSlackApp
methods.function: Updates a bot's Slack app, for example after its manifest changed. The app runs it by hand and also automatically in the background.
methods.returns: outcome (updated, up to date, recreate required, pending admin approval, not connected, manager reauth required, insufficient scopes, rate limited, Slack rejected, unsupported harness or throttled), slackTeamId, workspaceName, slackError, retryAfterSeconds, oauthAuthorizeUrl, approvalRequestFiled

methods.name: UninstallGrokBotSlackApp
methods.function: Removes a bot's Slack app from its workspace. With forgetIfUnreachable the backend drops its record even if Slack cannot be reached.
methods.returns: outcome (removed, not connected, manager reauth required, rate limited, Slack rejected or unsupported harness), slackTeamId, slackError, retryAfterSeconds, forgotten, workspaceName

methods.name: GetGrokBotTeamsInstallState
methods.function: Reports the Microsoft Teams install state of a bot's app: tenant, installed teams, admin approval status and any failure. It looks like the Teams counterpart of GetGrokBotSlackInstallState.
methods.returns: state (not connected, connected, app created, pending admin approval, installed, update pending, removed in Teams, removed, unsupported harness, not published or unavailable), tenantId, tenantDisplayName, catalogAppId, managerIsAdmin, installedTeams, approvalRequestFiledAtMs, rejectionNote, packageDownloadUrl, failureReason, teamAdminGrant (grantedByDisplayName, grantedAtMs, tenantId), tenants
methods.notes: Probe with the primary bot id returned 404 not_found, 'Resource not found.' Since 0.71.2 the desktop app calls it on its own and after install steps, to read the tenant, catalog app id and installed teams.

methods.name: ListGrokBotTeamsJoinedTeams
methods.function: Lists the Microsoft Teams teams the user has joined, to pick where the bot's Teams app goes. When a Microsoft tenant has to be chosen first, it returns the tenants instead (likely when the account spans more than one).
methods.returns: teams (teamId, displayName), tenants (tenantId, tenantDisplayName, adminConsent, managerAuthUpdatedAtMs)
methods.notes: New in 0.71.2. The app treats a non-empty tenants list as 'tenant required', drops teams with an empty id and shows the team id when the name is empty. Not probed.

methods.name: StartGrokBotTeamsConnect
methods.function: Starts the Microsoft consent step for a bot's Teams app. It returns a consent URL and a nonce.
methods.inputs: agentId, requestAdminScopes (true or false), grantScopeTeam (true or false)
methods.returns: consentUrl, nonce
methods.notes: Since 0.71.2 the desktop app calls it (grantScopeTeam defaults to false) and treats an empty consent URL as an error; unsupported_harness and not_published arrive as a failed_precondition detail. The Slack version of this step opens the returned URL in the browser.

methods.name: InstallGrokBotTeamsApp
methods.function: Installs the bot's Teams app into a Microsoft tenant, into chosen Teams teams and optionally for the user's personal scope.
methods.inputs: agentId, tenantId (optional), teamIds, installPersonal (true or false)
methods.returns: state, failureReason, tenants (tenantId, tenantDisplayName, adminConsent, managerAuthUpdatedAtMs)
methods.notes: Since 0.71.2 the desktop app calls it. A non-empty tenants list means a tenant must be picked first; otherwise the state decides the result, and pending admin approval or installed is followed by a GetGrokBotTeamsInstallState read. not_connected, not_installed, tenant_required, unsupported_harness and not_published can also arrive as a failed_precondition error detail. 'Teams' here means Microsoft Teams teams, not Grok Bot teams.

methods.name: ReinstallGrokBotTeamsApp
methods.function: Reinstalls a bot's Teams app in a tenant, probably to update it. The Slack version of this call updates the app manifest.
methods.returns: state, failureReason, tenants
methods.notes: Since 0.71.2 the desktop app calls it with agentId only: installed or update pending counts as updated, pending admin approval is followed by an install-state read, and a failureReason is a failure. The 'update' purpose is inferred from the Slack call and the UPDATE_PENDING state.

methods.name: UninstallGrokBotTeamsApp
methods.function: Removes a bot's Teams app. The response says if removal from the org catalog is waiting for a Teams admin.
methods.returns: state, catalogRemovalPendingAdmin (true or false)
methods.notes: Since 0.71.2 the desktop app calls it; only the state 'removed' counts as success, and it passes catalogRemovalPendingAdmin on to the screen.

methods.name: AddGrokBotTeamsAppToTeam
methods.function: Adds an already installed Teams app to more Microsoft Teams teams, and optionally to the personal scope.
methods.inputs: agentId, teamId, teamIds, installPersonal (true or false)
methods.returns: team, teams (teamId, displayName, rscGranted, installedAtMs), failureReason, installedPersonal
methods.notes: Since 0.71.2 the desktop app calls it with agentId and a single teamId; it does not send teamIds or installPersonal.

methods.name: ListGrokBotUserFormVaultEntries
methods.function: Lists the values saved in the autofill vault for user forms, such as details the user chose to save when submitting a form.
methods.returns: entries: entryId, kind, label, extraKey, value, createdAtMs, lastUsedAtMs, originHost
methods.notes: Returns the saved values themselves. No call site in the desktop app. SubmitGrokBotUserForm has a saveToVault flag that probably feeds this vault.

methods.name: UpsertGrokBotUserFormVaultEntry
methods.function: Creates or updates one entry in the autofill vault.
methods.inputs: entry (entryId, kind, label, extraKey, value, originHost)
